words.ex_cn: 这个瓶子有一个软木塞。
words.en: Cork is a light, porous material obtained from the bark of the cork oak tree, used especially for making stoppers for bottles.

words.ex: The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye.
words.ex_cn: 角膜是眼睛透明的部分。
words.en: The transparent layer forming the front of the eye.

words.ex: Education is the cornerstone of a strong society.
words.ex_cn: 教育是强大社会的基石。
words.en: A cornerstone is an important quality or feature on which a particular thing depends or is based.

words.ex: He felt a corporal pain after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他感到身体上的疼痛。
words.en: A corporal is a non-commissioned officer in the army, above a private and below a sergeant. As an adjective, it refers to the body or physical condition.

words.ex: The corporation sells smartphones worldwide.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司向全球销售智能手机。
words.en: A corporation is a large company or group of companies that is controlled together as a single organization.

words.ex: The police found a corpse near the river.
words.ex_cn: 警察在河边发现了一具尸体。
words.en: A corpse is a dead body, especially the dead body of a human.

words.ex: They maintain correspondence through letters.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过信件保持通信联系。
words.en: Communication by exchanging letters with someone; a close similarity, connection, or equivalence.

words.ex: The correspondent reported the news from the city.
words.ex_cn: 记者从城市报道了新闻。
words.en: A correspondent is someone who reports news from a particular place or on a particular subject for a newspaper, magazine, or television or radio station.

words.ex: The boy walked down the long corridor.
words.ex_cn: 男孩走过了长长的走廊。
words.en: A corridor is a long passage in a building, with doors and rooms on one or both sides.

words.ex: The government punished the official for corruption.
words.ex_cn: 政府因贪污惩罚了那名官员。
words.en: Corruption is dishonest or illegal behavior, especially by people in positions of power.

words.ex: The cosmic rays come from outer space.
words.ex_cn: 宇宙射线来自外太空。
words.en: Relating to the universe or cosmos, especially as distinct from the earth.

words.tr: adj. 全世界的；四海一家的；
words.ex: This city has a cosmopolitan population.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市有着来自世界各地的人口。
words.en: A cosmopolitan place or society is full of people from many different countries and cultures.

words.ex: He loves to watch the cosmos at night.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在夜晚观看宇宙。
words.en: The cosmos refers to the universe seen as a well-ordered whole, or to any system or structure that is complex and orderly.

words.ex: The small room was cosy with a warm blanket and a cup of tea.
words.ex_cn: 这个小房间铺着温暖的毯子，喝着热茶，非常舒适。
words.en: A place or situation that is cosy is comfortable and warm.

words.tr: n. 有围栏的幼儿床；轻便小床；
words.ex: The baby sleeps in a cot beside the bed.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿睡在床边的婴儿床里。
words.en: A cot is a small bed for a baby, with high sides to prevent the baby from falling out.

words.ex: They live in a small cottage near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一座小村舍里。
words.en: A cottage is a small house, usually in the countryside.

words.ex: The councilor spoke at the town meeting.
words.ex_cn: 这位议员在镇会上发言了。
words.en: A councilor is a member of a council, especially one who is elected to represent a particular area or group of people.

words.ex: The councillor spoke at the town meeting.
words.ex_cn: 这位议员在镇会上发表了讲话。
words.en: A councillor is an elected member of a local government council.

words.tr:
n. 律师；劝告
v. 提供咨询；劝告
words.ex: He hired a counsel to defend him in court.
words.ex_cn: 他聘请了一名律师为他在法庭上辩护。
words.en: Counsel refers to the act of giving advice or guidance, especially in a legal context, or to the person who provides such advice.

words.tr: n. 顾问；咨询师；法律顾问；
words.ex: He asked his counselor for advice about his future.
words.ex_cn: 他向他的顾问咨询了关于未来的问题。
words.en: A counselor is a person whose job is to give advice to people who need it, especially advice on their personal problems.

words.ex: Apples are countable things.
words.ex_cn: 苹果是可数的东西。
words.en: Capable of being counted; denumerable.

words.tr:
n. 反击；还击
v. 反击；还击
words.ex: The team launched a counterattack after the opponent scored.
words.ex_cn: 对手进球后，球队发动了反击。
words.en: A counterattack is an attack that you make on someone who has attacked you, in order to defend yourself or to defeat them.

words.ex: The doctor prescribed a counterdrug to help with the withdrawal symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 医生开了一种解瘾药来帮助缓解戒断症状。
words.en: A drug or substance used to counteract the effects of another drug, especially illegal drugs.

words.ex: The countess hosted a lavish party at her estate.
words.ex_cn: 伯爵夫人在她的庄园里举办了一场奢华的派对。
words.en: A countess is a woman who holds the rank of count or earl in her own right or is the wife of a count or earl.

words.tr: n. 优惠券；息票；配给券
words.ex: He used a coupon to buy milk at half price.
words.ex_cn: 他用一张优惠券以半价买了牛奶。
words.en: A coupon is a piece of printed paper that allows you to pay less money than usual for a product, or to get it free.

words.ex: The courageous firefighter saved the child from the burning house.
words.ex_cn: 这位勇敢的消防员从着火的房子里救出了孩子。
words.en: Someone who is courageous shows courage.

words.ex: He was courteous to everyone he met.
words.ex_cn: 他对遇到的每个人都很有礼貌。
words.en: Someone who is courteous is polite and respectful to other people.

words.ex: He showed courtesy by holding the door open.
words.ex_cn: 他为别人扶着门，表现得很礼貌。
words.en: Courtesy is polite behavior, or a polite action or remark.

words.tr:
n. 懦夫；胆小鬼；胆怯者
adj. 胆小的；怯懦的
words.ex: He was a coward and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他是个懦夫，逃跑了。
words.en: A coward is someone who is easily frightened and avoids dangerous or difficult situations.

words.tr:
adj. 怯懦的；胆小的
adv. 胆怯地
words.ex: He was cowardly and ran away from the fight.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，逃跑了。
words.en: If you describe someone as cowardly, you disapprove of them because they are easily frightened and avoid dangerous or difficult situations.

words.ex: The cowboy rode his horse across the desert.
words.ex_cn: 牛仔骑着马穿过沙漠。
words.en: A cowboy is a man who herds cattle, traditionally in the western United States, and is often depicted as wearing a wide-brimmed hat and boots.

words.ex: He caught a crab at the beach.
words.ex_cn: 他在海滩上抓到一只蟹。
words.en: A crab is a sea creature with a flat round body covered by a shell, and five pairs of legs with large claws on the front pair. Crabs usually move sideways.

words.tr:
n. 裂缝；噼啪声；
v. 破裂；
words.ex: There is a small crack in the wall.
words.ex_cn: 墙上有一条小裂缝。
words.en: If something hard cracks, or if you crack it, it becomes slightly damaged, with lines appearing on its surface.

words.tr: n. 薄脆饼干；爆竹；迷人的姑娘；黑客
words.ex: He ate a cracker with cheese.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块饼干配奶酪。
words.en: A cracker is a thin, crisp biscuit which is often eaten with cheese, or a person who is very good at something, especially solving problems or puzzles.

words.ex: The baby was sleeping in the cradle.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在吊架里睡觉。
words.en: A cradle is a small bed for a baby, which can be rocked from side to side. It can also refer to the place or period in which something begins or is developed.

words.ex: The craftsman made a wooden chair by hand.
words.ex_cn: 这位工匠手工制作了一把木椅。
words.en: A craftsman is a skilled worker who makes things by hand.

words.ex: The crafty fox stole the chicken at night.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸在夜里偷了鸡。
words.en: If you describe someone as crafty, you mean they are clever at achieving their aims by indirect or deceitful methods.

words.ex: The climber scaled the steep crag.
words.ex_cn: 攀岩者爬上了陡峭的岩壁。
words.en: A crag is a steep, rugged rock or cliff.

words.ex: The crane lifted the heavy steel beam.
words.ex_cn: 起重机吊起了沉重的钢梁。
words.en: A crane is a large machine that moves heavy things by lifting them in the air. It is also a large bird with long legs and a long neck.

words.tr:
n. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
v. 碰撞；坠毁；崩溃；
words.ex: The car crash happened at the intersection.
words.ex_cn: 汽车碰撞发生在十字路口。
words.en: If a vehicle crashes or if the driver crashes it, it hits something and is damaged or destroyed.

words.tr: n. 板条箱；箱子；篓；破旧的飞机或汽车；
words.ex: The apples were packed in a wooden crate.
words.ex_cn: 苹果被装在一个木板条箱里。
words.en: A crate is a large box used for transporting or storing goods.

words.ex: The baby is crawling on the floor.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿正在地板上爬。
words.en: To move slowly on hands and knees or by dragging the body close to the ground.

words.ex: The new dance became a craze among teenagers.
words.ex_cn: 这种新舞蹈在青少年中成为了一种狂热。
words.en: A craze is an activity, object, or idea that is extremely popular, usually for a short time.

words.tr: adj. 含乳脂的；奶油色的；乳脂状的
words.ex: The soup has a creamy texture.
words.ex_cn: 这汤有奶油般的质地。
words.en: Something that is creamy contains a lot of cream or is similar to cream in texture or color.

words.ex: The creditor asked for the money back.
words.ex_cn: 债权人要求把钱还回来。
words.en: A creditor is a person or organization to whom money is owed.

words.ex: He is credulous and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很轻信，相信他听到的每一个故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as credulous, you have a low opinion of them because they are too ready to believe what people tell them and are easily deceived.

words.ex: His creed is to always tell the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他的信条是永远说真话。
words.en: A creed is a set of beliefs, principles, or opinions that strongly influence the way people live or work.

words.ex: The children played near the creek after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在小河旁玩耍。
words.en: A creek is a small, narrow stream or river.

words.ex: The cat creeps slowly toward the bird.
words.ex_cn: 猫蹑手蹑脚地向鸟靠近。
words.en: To move slowly and quietly, especially in a way that does not attract attention.

words.tr:
n. 冠；顶部
v. 到达顶部；到达最高点
words.ex: The rooster has a bright red crest.
words.ex_cn: 公鸡有一个鲜红的冠。
words.en: The highest part of a hill or mountain; the top of a wave; a tuft or growth of feathers or skin on the head of a bird or other animal.

words.tr:
n. 饲料槽；有栏小卧床
v. 抄袭
words.ex: The horse eats hay from the crib.
words.ex_cn: 马从饲料槽里吃干草。
words.en: A crib is a bed with high sides for a baby or very young child. It can also mean to copy someone else's work and present it as your own.

words.ex: He plays cricket every weekend with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他每个周末都和朋友们打板球。
words.en: Cricket is a sport played between two teams of eleven players each, using a bat and ball, on a field with a wicket at each end.

words.tr: adj. 深红色的；绯红色的；
words.ex: The sky turned crimson at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 日落时，天空变成了深红色。
words.en: A deep red color that is slightly purplish, often associated with blood or a blush.

words.tr:
n. 跛子；（身体部分或全部肢体）有缺陷的人
v. 使成瘸子；严重损坏（削弱）
words.ex: The cripple walked slowly with a cane.
words.ex_cn: 那个跛子拄着拐杖慢慢走。
words.en: If someone is crippled by an injury, it is so serious that they can never move their body properly again. A cripple is a person who is severely disabled or unable to walk because of damage to their body.

words.ex: The country is facing an economic crisis.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家正面临经济危机。
words.en: A crisis is a situation in which something or someone is affected by one or more very serious problems.

words.ex: She ate a crisp apple for snack.
words.ex_cn: 她吃了一个脆苹果当点心。
words.en: Something that is crisp is hard, and makes a pleasant sound when you break it or crush it.

words.ex: The main criterion for winning is fairness.
words.ex_cn: 获胜的主要标准是公平。
words.en: A criterion is a principle or standard by which something may be judged or decided.

words.ex: The critic praised the new movie.
words.ex_cn: 这位评论家称赞了这部新电影。
words.en: A critic is a person who expresses opinions about the good and bad qualities of books, films, music, etc.

words.ex: He received criticism for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迟到而受到批评。
words.en: Criticism is the act of expressing disapproval of someone or something and of the faults they have or the mistakes they have made.

words.ex: He often criticizes his brother for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他经常批评他弟弟迟到。
words.en: If you criticize someone or something, you express your disapproval of them by saying what you think is wrong with them.

words.ex: The teacher criticise the student for not doing homework.
words.ex_cn: 老师批评学生没有做作业。
words.en: If you criticise someone or something, you express your disapproval of them by saying what you think is wrong with them.

words.ex: The crocodile is swimming in the river.
words.ex_cn: 鳄鱼正在河里游泳。
words.en: A crocodile is a large reptile that lives in rivers in the tropical regions of Africa, Asia, America, and Australia. It has a long body, a long tail, and very strong jaws.

words.tr:
n. 多方面求证；反复查对
v. 交叉核对；反复核对
words.ex: He crosscheck the numbers with the report.
words.ex_cn: 他把数字与报告进行了核对。
words.en: To verify (something) by comparing it with more than one source of information.

words.tr:
v. 蹲伏；蜷缩
n. 蹲伏；蜷缩
words.ex: The cat crouched low to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 猫蹲伏下来抓老鼠。
words.en: If you crouch, you bend your legs so that you are close to the ground and leaning forward slightly.

words.ex: A crow sat on the tree branch.
words.ex_cn: 一只乌鸦坐在树枝上。
words.en: A crow is a large black bird which makes a loud, harsh noise. If someone crows, they talk in a very proud way about something they have done or achieved.

words.ex: The queen wore a golden crown on her head.
words.ex_cn: 女王头上戴着一顶金皇冠。
words.en: A crown is a circular ornament, usually made of gold and jewels, which a king or queen wears on their head at official ceremonies. It can also refer to the top part of something, such as a tooth or a hill, or to the act of making someone a king or queen by placing a crown on their head.

words.ex: He lived in a crude hut with no electricity.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个没有电的简陋小屋里。
words.en: A crude substance or product is in its natural state and has not been processed or refined.

words.ex: The cruiser sailed slowly across the ocean.
words.ex_cn: 巡洋舰缓缓驶过海洋。
words.en: A cruiser is a large fast warship, or a large motorboat used for pleasure trips.

words.ex: A crumb fell on the table after he ate the bread.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完面包后，掉了一小块碎屑在桌子上。
words.en: A crumb is a very small piece of bread, cake, or biscuit.

words.ex: The old wall began to crumble after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 旧墙在雨后开始坍塌。
words.en: If something crumbles, or if you crumble it, it breaks into a lot of small pieces.

words.ex: He joined a crusade for clean water.
words.ex_cn: 他参加了一场为清洁用水而发起的运动。
words.en: A crusade is a long and determined attempt to achieve something that you strongly believe in, especially to bring about social or political change.

words.ex: He crushed the can with his hand.
words.ex_cn: 他用手把罐子压碎了。
words.en: To crush something means to press it very hard so that its shape is destroyed or so that it breaks into pieces. It can also mean to defeat someone completely, or to make someone feel extremely upset or disappointed.

words.ex: The earth's crust is made of rock.
words.ex_cn: 地球的地壳由岩石组成。
words.en: The crust is the hard outer layer of something, such as bread or the Earth's surface.

words.ex: He walks with a crutch after his accident.
words.ex_cn: 他事故后拄着拐杖走路。
words.en: A crutch is a stick with a handle and a part that fits under the arm, which you use to support your body if you are having difficulty in walking because of a foot or leg injury.

words.ex: She wears a necklace made of crystal.
words.ex_cn: 她戴一条水晶制成的项链。
words.en: A crystal is a solid that has a regular, repeating arrangement of atoms. Crystals are often transparent and can be used in jewelry or as decorative objects.

words.ex: The child played with a wooden cube.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩了一个木制立方体。
words.en: A cube is a solid object with six square faces which are all the same size.

words.ex: The box has a cubic shape.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子是立方体形状的。
words.en: Relating to or involving the cube or cubes.

words.ex: The teacher gave a cue to start the game.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了开始游戏的提示。
words.en: A cue is a signal for someone to do something, or a piece of information that helps someone to understand something.

words.tr:
n. 袖口；裤子翻边；巴掌；手铐
v. 给...上袖口（或翻边）；用手掌轻拍；用巴掌打
words.ex: He rolled up his cuff to wash his hands.
words.ex_cn: 他卷起袖口来洗手。
words.en: The part at the end of a sleeve, where the material of the sleeve is turned back or a separate band is sewn on. Also, to fasten someone's hands together with a pair of handcuffs.

words.ex: Italian cuisine is famous for pasta and pizza.
words.ex_cn: 意大利烹调风格以意大利面和披萨闻名。
words.en: A style or method of cooking, especially as characteristic of a particular country, region, or establishment.

words.tr: adj. 栽培的；耕作的； v. 栽培；“cultivate”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The cultivated vegetables taste better than wild ones.
words.ex_cn: 栽培的蔬菜比野生的更好吃。
words.en: If you describe someone as cultivated, you mean they are well educated and have good manners.

words.tr:
adj. 狡猾的；奸诈的；巧妙的
n. 奸诈；狡猾
words.ex: The cunning fox tricked the chicken.
words.ex_cn: 那只狡猾的狐狸骗了鸡。
words.en: Someone who is cunning is clever and good at deceiving others in order to get what they want.

words.tr: adj. 可医治的；可治愈的
words.ex: This disease is curable with medicine.
words.ex_cn: 这种病可以通过药物治愈。
words.en: A curable disease or medical condition is one that can be cured.

words.ex: He tried to curb his horse with the reins.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用缰绳勒住马。
words.en: If you curb something, you control it and keep it within limits.

words.ex: The child's curiosity made him ask many questions.
words.ex_cn: 孩子的好奇心让他问了很多问题。
words.en: A desire to know or learn about something; something that is interesting because it is unusual or strange.

words.ex: She curls her hair every morning.
words.ex_cn: 她每天早上卷头发。
words.en: To form into a spiral or curved shape; a piece of hair that grows in a curved shape.

words.ex: The currency in Japan is the yen.
words.ex_cn: 日本的货币是日元。
words.en: The system of money in general use in a particular country.

words.ex: He eats curry every Friday night.
words.ex_cn: 他每周五晚上吃咖喱。
words.en: Curry refers to a variety of dishes originating in the Indian subcontinent that use a complex combination of spices or herbs, usually including ground turmeric, cumin, coriander, ginger, and fresh or dried chilies. It also refers to the act of grooming a horse with a special comb.

words.ex: The old man muttered a curse under his breath.
words.ex_cn: 老人低声嘟囔了一句诅咒。
words.en: A curse is a word or sentence that is used to wish evil or harm on someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 可恶的； v. “curse”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This cursed rain ruined my picnic.
words.ex_cn: 这该死的雨毁了我的野餐。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is cursed, you mean that they seem to be under a curse or to bring bad luck.

words.tr:
n. 弯曲；曲线；
v. （使）弯成弧形；
words.ex: The road has a sharp curve ahead.
words.ex_cn: 前面的路有一个急转弯。
words.en: A curve is a smooth, gradually bending line, for example part of the edge of a circle.

words.ex: The mother won custody of her child.
words.ex_cn: 母亲获得了孩子的监护权。
words.en: Custody is the legal right or duty to care for someone or something, especially a child after its parents have separated or died.

words.ex: The cyclone destroyed many houses near the coast.
words.ex_cn: 气旋摧毁了沿海的许多房屋。
words.en: A cyclone is a violent tropical storm in which the air goes round and round.

words.ex: The engine has four cylinders.
words.ex_cn: 发动机有四个气缸。
words.en: A cylinder is a geometric figure with straight parallel sides and a circular or oval cross section.

words.tr: adj. 愤世嫉俗的；悲观的；
words.ex: He gave a cynical smile when they talked about honesty.
words.ex_cn: 当他们谈到诚实时，他露出了愤世嫉俗的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as cynical, you mean they believe that people always act selfishly.

words.ex: The czar ruled Russia with strong power.
words.ex_cn: 沙皇以强大的权力统治俄罗斯。
words.en: A czar is a male monarch or emperor, especially one of the former emperors of Russia.

words.tr:
v. 轻拍；轻触；轻敷
n. 轻拍；少量；能手；比目鱼
words.ex: He dabbed paint on the wall with a brush.
words.ex_cn: 他用刷子在墙上点了一些颜料。
words.en: To dab means to touch something lightly and quickly, often with a cloth or your fingers, in order to clean it, dry it, or apply something to it.

words.ex: He drew a dagger from his belt.
words.ex_cn: 他从腰带上抽出一把匕首。
words.en: A dagger is a weapon like a very short sword, used for stabbing.

words.tr:
adj. 该死的；可恶的；糟透的
v. 咒骂（某人下地狱）
words.ex: It's a damn good idea.
words.ex_cn: 这是个该死的好主意。
words.en: If you say that someone is damned if they do something, you mean that they will be in a very difficult situation if they do it.

words.tr:
adj. 该死的；可恶的；糟透的
v. 咒骂；“damn”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: He is damned for lying to his friends.
words.ex_cn: 他因为对朋友撒谎而遭到责骂。
words.en: Used to express anger, frustration, or contempt, or to emphasize a statement.

words.ex: The ground is damp after the rain.
words.ex_cn: 雨后地面是潮湿的。
words.en: Something that is damp is slightly wet, often in a way that is unpleasant.

words.ex: The keys dangle from his belt.
words.ex_cn: 钥匙挂在他的腰带上。
words.en: If something dangles from somewhere or if you dangle it somewhere, it hangs or swings loosely.

words.ex: The sky will darken before the storm.
words.ex_cn: 风暴来临前，天空会变暗。
words.en: To make or become dark or darker.

words.tr:
v. （使）突然移动；快速投掷；
n. 镖；
words.ex: The cat darted across the room.
words.ex_cn: 猫突然冲过房间。
words.en: A dart is a small, narrow object with a sharp point which can be thrown or shot. It can also mean to move suddenly and quickly in a particular direction.

words.ex: Add a dash of salt to the soup.
words.ex_cn: 给汤里加一点盐。
words.en: If you dash somewhere, you run or go there quickly and suddenly. A dash is a straight, horizontal line used in writing, for example to separate two main clauses whose meanings are closely connected.

words.ex: The birds sing at daybreak.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黎明时鸣叫。
words.en: The time in the morning when light first appears; dawn.

words.tr:
v. 使发昏；使迷乱
n. 恍惚； 晕眩
words.ex: The loud noise dazed him for a moment.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音让他一时发昏。
words.en: If someone is in a daze, they are feeling confused and unable to think clearly, often because they have had a shock or surprise.

words.tr:
v. 使目眩；使眼花；使惊叹
n. 耀眼；眩惑；灿烂
words.ex: The stars dazzle at night.
words.ex_cn: 夜晚的星星闪耀夺目。
words.en: If something dazzles you, it is so bright that you cannot see properly for a short time. It can also mean to greatly impress someone.

words.ex: He finished his homework before the deadline.
words.ex_cn: 他在截止日期前完成了作业。
words.en: A deadline is a time or date before which a particular task must be finished or a particular thing must be done.

words.ex: The old machine is a deadweight on the factory's progress.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器是工厂进步的重负。
words.en: The total weight that a ship can carry, including the cargo, fuel, passengers, and crew, but not including the weight of the ship itself.

words.ex: The loud music deafened him.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的音乐让他耳聋了。
words.en: If a noise deafens you, it is so loud that you cannot hear anything else at the same time.

words.ex: The dean gave a speech at the graduation ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 院长在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。
words.en: A dean is a senior official in a college or university, who is in charge of a faculty or department or a group of students.

words.tr: adj. 致命的；死一般的；非常
words.ex: The poison caused a deathly silence in the room.
words.ex_cn: 这种毒药让房间里陷入致命的寂静。
words.en: Something that is deathly is extremely serious or dangerous, often causing death. It can also describe something that resembles death in its appearance or effect.

words.ex: The debtor paid back the money last week.
words.ex_cn: 债务人上周还了钱。
words.en: A debtor is a person, organization, or country that owes money.

words.tr:
n. 首次露面；初次登场
v. 初次登场；首次推出
words.ex: He made his debut on stage last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚在舞台上首次登台。
words.en: The debut of a performer or sports player is their first public performance, appearance, or recording.

words.ex: He lived in Paris for a decade.
words.ex_cn: 他在巴黎生活了十年。
words.en: A decade is a period of ten years, especially one that begins with a year ending in 0, for example 1980 to 1989.

words.tr:
n. 腐烂；衰落；
v. 腐烂；
words.ex: The fruit began to show signs of decay.
words.ex_cn: 这水果开始出现腐烂的迹象。
words.en: To decay means to be slowly destroyed by a natural process or to become gradually worse in quality, condition, or strength.

words.tr: adj. 死去了的；已死的；亡故的； v. “decease”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The deceased man was buried last week.
words.ex_cn: 这位已故的男子上周被埋葬了。
words.en: Someone who is deceased has died.

words.ex: His deceit made his friends lose trust in him.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗让朋友们失去了对他的信任。
words.en: Deceit is behaviour that is intended to make someone believe something that is not true.

words.ex: He gave a deceitful smile to hide his lie.
words.ex_cn: 他露出一个虚伪的微笑来掩盖他的谎言。
words.en: If you say that someone is deceitful, you mean that they behave in a dishonest way by making other people believe something that is not true.

words.ex: His deception fooled everyone at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他的欺骗骗过了派对上的所有人。
words.en: Deception is the act of deceiving someone or the state of being deceived.

words.ex: The deceptive smile hid his true intentions.
words.ex_cn: 那欺骗性的微笑隐藏了他真正的意图。
words.en: If something is deceptive, it encourages you to believe something which is not true.

words.ex: The noise was 80 decibels.
words.ex_cn: 噪音是80分贝。
words.en: A decibel is a unit used to measure the intensity of a sound or the power level of an electrical signal by comparing it with a given level on a logarithmic scale.

words.tr: adv. 断然地；果断地；明确地；
words.ex: He decidedly refused to join the project.
words.ex_cn: 他断然拒绝参加这个项目。
words.en: In a way that is clear and definite; undoubtedly.

words.tr:
adj. 小数的；十进位的
n. 小数
words.ex: The decimal point separates the whole number from the decimal part.
words.ex_cn: 小数点将整数部分与小数部分分开。
words.en: A decimal is a fraction that is written in a special form. It is based on powers of ten, and it uses a decimal point to separate the whole number part from the fractional part.

words.ex: His decisive action saved the team.
words.ex_cn: 他果断的行动拯救了团队。
words.en: If a fact, action, or event is decisive, it makes it certain that there will be a particular result.

words.ex: The country made a declaration of independence.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家发表了独立宣言。
words.en: A declaration is a formal statement or announcement.

words.ex: He can decode the secret message.
words.ex_cn: 他能译解这个秘密信息。
words.en: To convert coded data into intelligible form.

words.ex: She bought new decoration for her living room.
words.ex_cn: 她为客厅买了新的装饰品。
words.en: Decoration is the process or art of decorating something, or the objects used to decorate something.

words.tr: adj. 装饰性的；作装饰用的；
words.ex: The room has decorative flowers on the table.
words.ex_cn: 房间里桌上有一些装饰性的花。
words.en: Something that is decorative is intended to look pretty or attractive.

words.tr:
n. 减少；
v. 减少；降低；
words.ex: There was a decrease in rainfall last month.
words.ex_cn: 上个月降雨量减少了。
words.en: If something decreases or you decrease it, it becomes less in quantity, size, or intensity.

words.tr:
n. 法令；判决
v. 判决；颁布；裁定
words.ex: The king issued a decree to stop the war.
words.ex_cn: 国王发布了一项法令来停止战争。
words.en: An official order issued by a legal authority.

words.ex: He deducts tax from his salary every month.
words.ex_cn: 他每月从工资中扣除税款。
words.en: If you deduct an amount from a total, you subtract it from the total.

words.ex: His deduction was based on the evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他的推论基于证据。
words.en: A deduction is a conclusion that you reach about something because of other things that you know to be true.

words.ex: The default setting is on.
words.ex_cn: 默认设置是开启的。
words.en: If a person, company, or country defaults on something that they have legally agreed to do, such as paying a debt or keeping to an agreement, they fail to do it.

words.ex: The defect in the phone made it hard to use.
words.ex_cn: 手机的缺陷让它很难使用。
words.en: A defect is a fault or imperfection in a person or thing.

words.ex: The defendant spoke calmly in court.
words.ex_cn: 被告在法庭上平静地发言。
words.en: A defendant is a person or entity against whom a criminal or civil action is brought in a court of law.

words.tr: n. 防御者；防守队员；拥护者；卫冕者
words.ex: The defender stopped the ball with his foot.
words.ex_cn: 防守球员用脚挡住了球。
words.en: A defender is someone who defends a place or person, or who supports an idea or policy.

words.tr: adj. 可防御的；可保卫的；可辩护的
words.ex: The small castle was defensible with high walls.
words.ex_cn: 这座小城堡有高墙，易于防守。
words.en: Able to be defended or justified.

words.ex: The boy showed defiance by refusing to follow the rules.
words.ex_cn: 男孩通过拒绝遵守规则来表现违抗。
words.en: Defiance is behaviour or an attitude which shows that you are not willing to obey someone or something.

words.ex: The defiant child refused to clean his room.
words.ex_cn: 这个不顺从的孩子拒绝打扫房间。
words.en: If you say that someone is defiant, you mean they show aggression or independence by refusing to obey someone.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；缺乏的；有缺陷的
words.ex: The plant is deficient in sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 这株植物缺乏阳光。
words.en: If someone or something is deficient in a particular thing, they do not have the full amount of it that they need.

words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.ex: The mirror deflects the light to the wall.
words.ex_cn: 镜子把光线反射到墙上。
words.en: If you deflect something such as criticism or attention, you act in a way that prevents it from being directed towards you or affecting you.

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.

words.ex: The delegation met with the president yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 代表团昨天会见了总统。
words.en: A delegation is a group of people who have been sent somewhere to have talks with other people on behalf of a larger group of people.

words.ex: He will delete the old file.
words.ex_cn: 他会删除那个旧文件。
words.en: To delete something means to remove it or erase it.

words.ex: I bought sandwich meat from the deli.
words.ex_cn: 我从熟食店买了三明治肉。
words.en: A deli is a shop where you can buy foods such as cooked meats, cheeses, and salads.

words.tr:
adj. 深思熟虑的；故意的；
v. 深思熟虑；
words.ex: He made a deliberate choice to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他深思熟虑后决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you do something that is deliberate, you planned or decided to do it beforehand, and so it happens on purpose rather than by chance.

words.ex: The restaurant serves a famous delicacy called seafood soup.
words.ex_cn: 这家餐厅供应一道著名的佳肴，叫海鲜汤。
words.en: Delicacy refers to the quality of being delicate, fine, or subtle in appearance, structure, or manner. It can also denote a choice or rare food item.

words.ex: He bought ham and cheese at the delicatessen.
words.ex_cn: 他在熟食店买了火腿和奶酪。
words.en: A delicatessen is a shop where foods such as cooked meats, cheeses, and unusual or foreign foods are sold.

words.ex: The boy's delinquency worried his parents.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的犯罪行为让他的父母很担心。
words.en: Delinquency refers to minor crimes, especially those committed by young people.

words.tr:
adj. 失职的；违法的；拖欠债务的
n. 违犯者；少年罪犯；违法者
words.ex: The delinquent worker ignored his duties.
words.ex_cn: 这位失职的员工忽视了他的职责。
words.en: A delinquent is someone, especially a young person, who commits a crime or breaks the law.

words.ex: The Nile River forms a large delta before it flows into the sea.
words.ex_cn: 尼罗河在流入大海之前形成了一个巨大的三角洲。
words.en: A delta is an area of low, flat land shaped like a triangle, where a river splits and spreads out into several branches before entering the sea.

words.ex: He has a delusion that he is a famous singer.
words.ex_cn: 他有一种错觉，认为自己是一位著名歌手。
words.en: A delusion is a belief or impression that is firmly maintained despite being contradicted by what is generally accepted as reality or rational argument, typically a symptom of mental disorder.

words.tr: n. 煽动民情；蛊惑民心
words.ex: He used demagogy to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 他用煽动性言论赢得了选举。
words.en: Demagogy is the practice of gaining political support by arousing the emotions, passions, and prejudices of the people rather than by using rational argument.

words.tr: adj. 要求高的；费力的； v. 需要；“demand”的现在分词；
words.ex: The job is demanding because it needs long hours and high focus.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作要求高，因为它需要长时间工作和高度专注。
words.en: Requiring much effort or attention; exacting.

words.ex: He got a demerit for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而被扣分。
words.en: A demerit is a fault or disadvantage.

words.ex: People vote in democracy to choose their leaders.
words.ex_cn: 人们在民主制度下投票选择他们的领导人。
words.en: A system of government by the whole population or all the eligible members of a state, typically through elected representatives.

words.tr: n. 民主主义者；民主党员；
words.ex: He is a democrat who believes in equal rights for all.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位相信所有人平等权利的民主主义者。
words.en: A democrat is someone who believes in the principles of democracy, such as the idea that everyone should have an equal say in how their country is governed.

words.ex: They will demolish the old building next week.
words.ex_cn: 他们下周会拆掉那座旧建筑。
words.en: To demolish something such as a building means to destroy it completely. It can also mean to defeat someone completely in a discussion, argument, or competition.

words.ex: The teacher gave a demonstration of how to solve the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师演示了如何解这道数学题。
words.en: A demonstration is a public meeting or march in which people show their opposition to something or their support for something.

words.tr:
adj. 明白表示的；证实的；公然表示情绪的
n. 指示词
words.ex: He is demonstrative with his love for his family.
words.ex_cn: 他对家人表达爱意时很外露。
words.en: If you are demonstrative, you show your feelings or behave in a way that shows your love for someone.

words.ex: The lion returned to its den at night.
words.ex_cn: 狮子晚上回到了它的兽穴。
words.en: A den is the home of certain types of wild animals such as lions or foxes, or a place where someone feels safe and private.

words.ex: His denial of the mistake made everyone angry.
words.ex_cn: 他否认错误，让所有人都生气了。
words.en: A denial is a statement that something is not true or does not exist.

words.ex: There are many denominations in Christianity.
words.ex_cn: 基督教中有许多宗派。
words.en: A denomination is a recognized autonomous branch of the Christian Church or a unit of value, especially in currency.

words.ex: The denominator is 5 in the fraction 3/5.
words.ex_cn: 在分数 3/5 中，分母是 5。
words.en: The number below the line in a fraction that shows the number of equal parts into which the whole is divided.

words.ex: The symbol x denotes an unknown number.
words.ex_cn: 符号 x 表示一个未知数。
words.en: If one thing denotes another, it is a sign or indication of it.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.ex: The forest is dense with trees.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林树木茂密。
words.en: Something that is dense contains a lot of things or people in a small area.

words.ex: The trees grow densely in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 树木在森林里浓密地生长。
words.en: In a manner that is closely compacted in substance; thickly.

words.ex: The density of water is 1 gram per cubic centimeter.
words.ex_cn: 水的密度是每立方厘米1克。
words.en: Density is a measure of how much mass is contained in a given unit volume of a substance.

words.ex: He went to the dental clinic for a check-up.
words.ex_cn: 他去牙科诊所做检查。
words.en: Relating to the teeth or to the work of a dentist.

words.tr: n. 牙托； 一副假牙
words.ex: He wears a denture to eat food.
words.ex_cn: 他戴假牙来吃东西。
words.en: A denture is a removable plate or frame holding one or more artificial teeth.

words.ex: He denies taking the money.
words.ex_cn: 他否认拿了钱。
words.en: To deny means to declare that something is not true, or to refuse to give or grant something.

words.ex: The departure of the train was at 8 p.m.
words.ex_cn: 火车的出发时间是晚上8点。
words.en: The act of leaving a place, especially at the start of a journey.

words.ex: He is a dependant of his parents.
words.ex_cn: 他是他父母的受赡养者。
words.en: A dependant is a person who relies on another, especially a family member, for financial support.

words.ex: The painting depicts a quiet village at sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画描绘了一个宁静的村庄在日落时分的景象。
words.en: To depict someone or something means to show or represent them in a work of art such as a drawing or painting.

words.tr: v. 驱逐出境；使举止得体
words.ex: They will deport him for breaking the law.
words.ex_cn: 他们将因他违法而驱逐他。
words.en: If a government deports someone, usually someone who is not a citizen of that country, it sends them out of the country because they have committed a crime or because it believes they do not have the right to be there.

words.tr: n. 沉积（物）；革职；宣誓证词；作证书
words.ex: Sediment deposition forms layers on the riverbed.
words.ex_cn: 沉积物在河床上形成层状结构。
words.en: The act of depositing something, especially a layer of a substance formed by natural processes, or the giving of testimony under oath.

words.ex: The car's depreciation is high after five years.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车五年后折旧很高。
words.en: A decrease in the value of a currency with respect to other currencies or a decrease in the value of an asset over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or age.

words.tr: v. 压下；降低；使沮丧；使不活泼；使萧条
words.ex: He depresses the button to start the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他按下按钮启动机器。
words.en: If something depresses you, it makes you feel sad and disappointed.

words.tr: adj. 令人抑郁的；令人沮丧的；令人消沉的； v. “depress”的现在分词；
words.ex: The rainy weather made the day feel depressing.
words.ex_cn: 阴雨的天气让这一天感觉令人抑郁。
words.en: Making someone feel very unhappy and without hope.

words.ex: The storm deprived us of electricity.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴剥夺了我们的电力。
words.en: If you deprive someone of something that they want or need, you take it away from them, or you prevent them from having it.

words.ex: The deputy signed the document for the manager.
words.ex_cn: 代理人替经理签署了文件。
words.en: A deputy is a person who is appointed to act as a substitute for another, especially in a position of authority.

words.ex: The old factory is now a derelict building.
words.ex_cn: 那座旧工厂现在是一座破败的建筑。
words.en: If a building or a piece of land is derelict, it is not cared for and is in bad condition. A derelict person or thing is one that has been abandoned or neglected.

words.ex: The derivation of this word is from Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这个词的起源是拉丁语。
words.en: Derivation refers to the process by which a word is formed from another word or from a root, especially by the addition of an affix.

words.ex: The cheese is a derivative of milk.
words.ex_cn: 这种奶酪是牛奶的派生物。
words.en: A derivative is something which has been developed or obtained from something else.

words.ex: He is a descendant of the first king.
words.ex_cn: 他是第一位国王的后裔。
words.en: A person, plant, or animal that is descended from a particular ancestor.

words.ex: The plane began its descent at 10,000 feet.
words.ex_cn: 飞机在一万英尺高度开始下降。
words.en: The act of moving or falling downward.

words.ex: The teacher gave a descriptive answer about the painting.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这幅画给出了一个描述性的回答。
words.en: If you describe something as descriptive, you mean that it gives a detailed account of something.

words.ex: The teacher designated him as the group leader.
words.ex_cn: 老师指派他为组长。
words.en: If you designate someone or something as a particular thing, you formally give them that description or name.

words.tr: n. 指明；标示；指定；称号
words.ex: His designation is manager at the company.
words.ex_cn: 他的职位是公司的经理。
words.en: A designation is a name, title, or description given to someone or something, especially one that is official or formal.

words.ex: He works on his desktop every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都在台式机上工作。
words.en: The top of a desk; a computer that is designed to be used on a desk.

words.ex: The desert looks desolate and empty.
words.ex_cn: 这片沙漠看起来荒凉而空旷。
words.en: If you describe a place as desolate, you mean that it is empty and looks sad because there are no people there or because it has been damaged.

words.tr: n. 荒凉；凄凉；悲痛；孤立无援
words.ex: The abandoned town was full of desolation.
words.ex_cn: 这座废弃的城镇满是荒凉。
words.en: Desolation refers to a state of complete emptiness or destruction, often evoking a sense of loneliness or despair.

words.ex: He despises lying.
words.ex_cn: 他鄙视撒谎。
words.en: If you despise something or someone, you dislike them and have a very low opinion of them.

words.tr: n. 暴君；专制统治者；专制君主
words.ex: The despot ruled the country with fear.
words.ex_cn: 暴君用恐惧统治国家。
words.en: A despot is a ruler or other person who holds absolute power, typically one who exercises it in a cruel or oppressive way.

words.ex: The stars destine her to be a leader.
words.ex_cn: 命运注定她将成为一位领导者。
words.en: To determine the future or the fate of something or someone in advance.

words.tr: adj. 命中注定的； v. “destine”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was destined to become a great teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他命中注定会成为一名伟大的老师。
words.en: If something is destined to happen or if someone is destined to behave in a particular way, it seems certain to happen or they seem certain to behave in that way, often because of fate or because it has been decided in advance.

words.ex: He believed his destiny was to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自己的命运是成为一名医生。
words.en: Destiny is the force which some people believe controls the things that happen to you in your life.

words.ex: The storm was destructive and broke many houses.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴具有破坏性，摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: Causing great and irreparable harm or damage.

words.ex: He tried to detach himself from the group.
words.ex_cn: 他试图脱离这个群体。
words.en: If you detach one thing from another that it is fixed to, you remove it. If one thing detaches from another, it becomes separated from it.

words.tr: adj. 分离的； v. 脱离；拆卸；分离；“detach”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The house is detached from the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子与邻居的房子是分开的。
words.en: If someone is detached, they do not have any emotional interest in a situation and therefore can make fair decisions.

words.tr: n. 分离；拆开；支队；超然；分遣队
words.ex: The detachment of the two teams caused confusion.
words.ex_cn: 两个团队的分离造成了混乱。
words.en: If you refer to someone's detachment, you mean that they do not become involved in other people's problems or emotions, or that they do not show their own feelings.

words.ex: The police will detain the suspect for questioning.
words.ex_cn: 警察将扣留嫌疑人进行审问。
words.en: If someone is detained, they are officially held in a place, especially a prison, and are not allowed to leave.

words.ex: I can detect a change in her mood.
words.ex_cn: 我能察觉到她情绪的变化。
words.en: To detect something means to find it or discover it, often using special equipment or methods.

words.ex: The detective solved the mystery with clues.
words.ex_cn: 侦探用线索破解了谜案。
words.en: A detective is someone whose job is to discover what has happened in a crime or other situation and to find the people involved.

words.tr: n. 探测器；检测器；发现者；
words.ex: The detector found a hidden metal object.
words.ex_cn: 探测器发现了一个隐藏的金属物体。
words.en: A detector is a device that is used to discover the presence of something, such as smoke, metal, or radiation.

words.tr: n. 洗涤剂；洗衣粉；去垢剂；
words.ex: She uses detergent to wash the clothes.
words.ex_cn: 她用洗涤剂洗衣服。
words.en: A detergent is a substance that is used for cleaning things, especially clothes and dishes.

words.ex: The weather will deteriorate tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天天气会恶化。
words.en: If something deteriorates, it becomes worse in some way.

words.ex: His determination helped him finish the race.
words.ex_cn: 他的决心帮助他完成了比赛。
words.en: Determination is the quality that you show when you have decided to do something and you will not let anything stop you.

words.ex: Smoking is a detriment to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that causes damage, harm, or loss.

words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.tr: adj. 恶魔似的；恶毒的；邪恶的；极度的
words.ex: The devilish boy laughed loudly.
words.ex_cn: 那个顽皮的男孩大声笑了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as devilish, you mean that they are evil or are connected with the devil. Also, you can use devilish to emphasize that something is very extreme or difficult.

words.ex: His devotion to his family is obvious.
words.ex_cn: 他对家庭的献身显而易见。
words.en: Devotion is great love, affection, or admiration for someone or something.

words.tr: v. 吞食；吞噬；狼吞虎咽地吃；如饥似渴地看
words.ex: The dog devoured the meat quickly.
words.ex_cn: 狗很快地把肉吃光了。
words.en: To eat something quickly and eagerly, especially because you are very hungry; to destroy something quickly and completely.

words.ex: Dew forms on the grass in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨露水出现在草地上。
words.en: Dew is small drops of water that form on the ground and other surfaces outside during the night.

words.ex: A dewdrop hangs on the grass at dawn.
words.ex_cn: 黎明时分，一滴露珠悬在草叶上。
words.en: A dewdrop is a drop of water that forms on cool surfaces at night, as a result of condensation.

words.ex: The doctor made a diagnosis after checking the symptoms.
words.ex_cn: 医生在检查了症状后做出了诊断。
words.en: The identification of the nature of an illness or other problem by examination of the symptoms.

words.ex: The doctor used a diagnostic test to find the problem.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用了一项诊断测试来找出问题。
words.en: Relating to the identification of the nature and cause of a phenomenon, especially a disease or other disorder.

words.ex: The diameter of the circle is 10 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的直径是10厘米。
words.en: A straight line passing from side to side through the center of a body or figure, especially a circle or sphere.

words.ex: The teacher gave a dictation of five sentences.
words.ex_cn: 老师进行了一次五句话的听写。
words.en: Dictation is the speaking or reading aloud of words for someone else to write down.

words.ex: The dictator ruled the country for many years.
words.ex_cn: 这位独裁者统治这个国家很多年。
words.en: A dictator is a ruler who has complete power in a country, especially when this power has been obtained by force and is used unfairly or cruelly.

words.tr: n. 独裁；专政；独裁政府；独裁国家
words.ex: The country suffered under a dictatorship.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家曾遭受独裁统治。
words.en: A dictatorship is a government or a social situation where one person makes all the rules and decisions without input from anyone else.

words.ex: He spoke with clear diction.
words.ex_cn: 他说话吐字清晰。
words.en: Diction refers to the choice and use of words and phrases in speech or writing, or the manner in which words are pronounced.

words.ex: The truck runs on diesel.
words.ex_cn: 这辆卡车使用柴油运行。
words.en: Diesel is a type of heavy oil used as fuel in diesel engines.

words.tr:
adj. 差别的；有区别的
n. 差别；差额；差价
words.ex: There is a differential cost between the two brands.
words.ex_cn: 这两个品牌之间有不同的价格。
words.en: A differential is a difference between things, especially between things that should be the same. In mathematics, a differential is an infinitesimal change in a variable.

words.tr:
v. 弥漫；
adj. 分散的；
words.ex: Smoke began to diffuse through the room.
words.ex_cn: 烟开始弥漫在整个房间里。
words.en: If something such as knowledge or information is diffused, or if it diffuses, it is made known over a wide area or to a lot of people.

words.tr: adj. 易消化的；易理解的
words.ex: The food is easy and digestible.
words.ex_cn: 这种食物容易消化。
words.en: Capable of being digested; easily digested.

words.ex: The digestive system breaks down food.
words.ex_cn: 消化系统分解食物。
words.en: Relating to the process of digesting food.

words.tr: n. 从0到9的任一数字；手指；脚趾；
words.ex: The password has four digits.
words.ex_cn: 这个密码有四位数字。
words.en: A digit is a written symbol for any of the numbers 0 to 9.

words.ex: The old man walked with a dignified posture.
words.ex_cn: 这位老人以有尊严的姿态行走。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is dignified, you mean they are calm, impressive and deserve respect.

words.tr: v. 使有尊严；使崇高；使显贵
words.ex: He tried to dignify his actions with excuses.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用借口来美化自己的行为。
words.en: To dignify something means to make it seem important and worthy of respect, often by treating it in a serious or formal way.

words.tr:
n. 堤坝；排水沟
v. 筑堤；开排水沟
words.ex: The dike was built to prevent flooding.
words.ex_cn: 修建堤坝是为了防止洪水泛滥。
words.en: A dike is a long wall or embankment built to prevent flooding from the sea or a river.

words.ex: He faced a dilemma: stay home or go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他面临一个困境：是待在家里还是去上班。
words.en: A situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives, especially equally undesirable ones.

words.ex: He shows diligence in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天认真完成作业。
words.en: Conscientiousness in paying proper attention to a task; giving the degree of care required in a given situation.

words.ex: He is diligent in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都很勤奋地做作业。
words.en: Someone who is diligent works hard and is careful and thorough.

words.tr:
v. 稀释
adj. 经稀释的
words.ex: He dilutes the juice with water.
words.ex_cn: 他用水稀释果汁。
words.en: To dilute a liquid means to make it thinner or weaker by adding water or another liquid to it.

words.tr:
adj. 暗淡的；昏暗的；模糊的
v. （使）变暗淡；（使）变模糊；（使）减弱
words.ex: The room is dim because the lights are off.
words.ex_cn: 房间很暗，因为灯关了。
words.en: If a light or a place is dim, it is not bright or is not lit very strongly.

words.ex: He found a dime on the ground.
words.ex_cn: 他在地上找到一枚一角硬币。
words.en: A dime is a coin worth ten cents, one tenth of a United States dollar.

words.ex: The dimension of the box is 10 cm by 5 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子的尺寸是10厘米乘5厘米。
words.en: A dimension is a measurement of something in a particular direction, or the scope or scale of something.

words.tr: adj. 维度的；空间的；尺寸的
words.ex: The box has three dimensional shapes.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子有三个维度的形状。
words.en: Relating to measurements in length, width, and height, or to the spatial extent of something.

words.ex: They dine at 7 every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他们每天晚上七点进餐。
words.en: To dine means to eat dinner.

words.ex: The child loves to watch dinosaurs on TV.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子喜欢在电视上看恐龙。
words.en: A dinosaur is a type of reptile that lived millions of years ago, known for its large size and often extinct species.

words.ex: Carbon dioxide makes the air warm.
words.ex_cn: 二氧化碳使空气变暖。
words.en: A compound containing two atoms of oxygen combined with another element or group.

words.tr: n. 毕业文凭；学位证书；
words.ex: He received his diploma last June.
words.ex_cn: 他去年六月拿到了毕业文凭。
words.en: A diploma is a document which may be awarded by a university or college, or by a high school, showing that someone has successfully completed a course of study.

words.tr: n. 外交；外交手腕；交际手段
words.ex: He uses diplomacy to solve the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 他用外交手段解决冲突。
words.en: Diplomacy is the activity of managing relations between the governments of different countries, especially in the context of international relations, negotiations, and treaties.

words.tr: n. 外交官；会耍手腕儿的人
words.ex: The diplomat met the president yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 这位外交官昨天会见了总统。
words.en: A diplomat is a person who represents their country in a foreign country, managing political relations and negotiations.

words.ex: I looked up his phone number in the directory.
words.ex_cn: 我在姓名地址录里查了他的电话号码。
words.en: A directory is a book or list which gives names, addresses, and other information about people or organizations.

words.ex: He is a diplomatic ambassador who handles international relations.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位处理国际关系的外交大使。
words.en: Diplomatic means relating to diplomacy or diplomats, or using skill and tact in dealing with people.

words.tr: n. 伤残；失去能力；无能力；
words.ex: He has a disability that makes walking difficult.
words.ex_cn: 他有伤残，导致行走困难。
words.en: A disability is a physical or mental condition that limits a person's movements, senses, or activities.

words.tr: adj. 处于不利地位的；贫困的； v. “disadvantage”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The school helps disadvantaged children with free meals.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校为处境不利的孩子提供免费餐食。
words.en: People who are disadvantaged do not have the same opportunities or advantages as other people, often because of their financial situation or social position.

words.ex: It is disadvantageous to skip breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 不吃早餐是不利的。
words.en: If something is disadvantageous to you, it is likely to cause you difficulties or problems.

words.ex: The smell was disagreeable.
words.ex_cn: 这气味令人不愉快。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as disagreeable, you mean that they are rather unpleasant.

words.ex: There was a disagreement about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 关于这个计划，他们产生了分歧。
words.en: A disagreement is a situation in which people have different opinions about something and often argue.

words.ex: He disappointed his parents by failing the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他考试不及格，让父母失望了。
words.en: If things or people disappoint you, they are not as good as you had hoped, or do not do what you expected them to do.

words.tr: adj. 失望的；沮丧的； v. “disappoint”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was disappointed when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 他考试没及格时感到很失望。
words.en: If you are disappointed, you are sad because something has not happened or because something is not as good as you had hoped.

words.tr: adj. 令人失望的；令人扫兴的； v. “disappoint”的现在分词；
words.ex: The movie was disappointing.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影令人失望。
words.en: If something is disappointing, it is not as good as you hoped it would be.

words.ex: He felt disappointment when he failed the test.
words.ex_cn: 当他考试没及格时，他感到失望。
words.en: A feeling of sadness or displeasure caused by the nonfulfillment of one's hopes or expectations.

words.ex: He showed his disapproval by staying silent.
words.ex_cn: 他通过保持沉默表示反对。
words.en: Disapproval is the feeling that someone or something is bad, wrong, or unacceptable.

words.tr: v. 不赞成；反对；不同意
words.ex: My parents disapprove of my choice.
words.ex_cn: 我的父母不赞成我的选择。
words.en: If you disapprove of something, you have a negative opinion of it, often because you think it is wrong or not suitable.

words.tr: v. 解除武装；缴械；裁减军备
words.ex: The soldier will disarm the bomb.
words.ex_cn: 士兵将拆除炸弹。
words.en: To disarm someone means to make them less hostile or suspicious by removing their weapons or by being friendly.

words.tr: n. 裁减军备；解除武装；缴械
words.ex: The two countries agreed on disarmament to reduce weapons.
words.ex_cn: 这两个国家同意进行裁军以减少武器。
words.en: The reduction or withdrawal of military forces and weapons.

words.ex: The storm caused disastrous damage to the village.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴给村庄造成了灾难性的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as disastrous, you mean that it is very unfortunate or unsuccessful.

words.ex: He stared at the money with disbelief.
words.ex_cn: 他难以置信地盯着那些钱。
words.en: Disbelief is the feeling of not being able to believe that something is true or real.

words.ex: He disbelieve the story about aliens.
words.ex_cn: 他不相信关于外星人的故事。
words.en: If you disbelieve someone or something, you do not believe that what they say is true or that they exist.

words.ex: He decided to discard his old habits.
words.ex_cn: 他决定抛开旧习惯。
words.en: To discard something means to get rid of it because you no longer want it or need it.

words.ex: He could discern a small bird in the trees.
words.ex_cn: 他能辨明树上有一只小鸟。
words.en: If you can discern something, you are aware of it and know what it is.

words.ex: He was a faithful disciple of the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是老师的一名忠实弟子。
words.en: A disciple is a follower or student of a teacher, leader, or philosopher.

words.ex: The school has a disciplinary policy for students who break rules.
words.ex_cn: 学校对违反规则的学生有纪律规定。
words.en: Relating to discipline; enforcing or administering discipline.

words.ex: He made a disclosure about the secret plan.
words.ex_cn: 他透露了这个秘密计划。
words.en: The act of making something known or the fact that is made known.

words.tr: n. 迪斯科舞会；迪斯科舞厅；
words.ex: We went to a disco last Saturday night.
words.ex_cn: 我们上个星期六晚上去了迪斯科舞会。
words.en: A disco is a club or party where people dance to pop music.

words.ex: He felt discontent with his job.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的工作感到不满。
words.en: Discontent is a feeling of being unhappy because you are not satisfied with your situation or with what you have.

words.ex: They had a discord about the movie ending.
words.ex_cn: 他们对电影的结局有分歧。
words.en: Disagreement or strife between people or groups.

words.ex: Don't discourage him from trying.
words.ex_cn: 不要阻止他尝试。
words.en: If someone or something discourages you, they cause you to lose your enthusiasm about your actions.

words.ex: His discourse on climate change was clear and logical.
words.ex_cn: 他关于气候变化的论述清晰而有逻辑。
words.en: Discourse is spoken or written communication between people, especially serious discussion of a particular subject.

words.ex: There is a discrepancy between the two reports.
words.ex_cn: 这两份报告之间有差异。
words.en: A discrepancy is a difference between two or more things that should be the same.

words.ex: The teacher gave students discretion to choose their own topic.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了学生自行选择题目的权利。
words.en: Discretion is the quality of behaving in a quiet and controlled way without drawing attention to yourself or giving away personal or private information.

words.ex: They discriminate against people because of their race.
words.ex_cn: 他们因为种族而歧视他人。
words.en: To discriminate means to recognize a distinction; differentiate. It can also mean to make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, sex, or age.

words.ex: He showed disdain for the lazy students.
words.ex_cn: 他对那些懒惰的学生表现出蔑视。
words.en: If you feel disdain for someone or something, you dislike them because you think that they are inferior or unimportant.

words.ex: The passengers disembark at the port.
words.ex_cn: 乘客们在港口上岸。
words.en: To disembark means to leave a ship, aircraft, or other vehicle.

words.ex: It was disgraceful to lie to your teacher.
words.ex_cn: 对老师撒谎是可耻的。
words.en: If you say that something is disgraceful, you are emphasizing that it is very bad or wrong, and that you find it completely unacceptable.

words.tr:
n. 伪装；伪装物；
v. 伪装；掩饰；
words.ex: He wore a hat and glasses as a disguise.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了帽子和眼镜作为伪装。
words.en: To disguise means to change your appearance or behavior so that people will not recognize you, or to make something seem different from what it really is.

words.ex: He felt disgust when he saw the dirty food.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到脏兮兮的食物时，他感到厌恶。
words.en: A feeling of revulsion or profound disapproval aroused by something unpleasant or offensive.

words.tr: adj. 令人厌恶的；令人作呕的； v. “disgust”的现在分词；
words.ex: The smell of the rotten food was disgusting.
words.ex_cn: 腐烂食物的气味令人厌恶。
words.en: If you say that something is disgusting, you mean that you find it completely unacceptable or unpleasant.

words.ex: He is dishonest when he lies about his homework.
words.ex_cn: 当他谎报作业时，他是不诚实的。
words.en: If you say that someone is dishonest, you mean that they are not honest and you cannot trust them.

words.tr: adj. 不名誉的；不光彩的；可耻的
words.ex: His actions were deemed dishonorable by his peers.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为被同僚们认为是不名誉的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as dishonorable, you mean that it is shameful or disgraceful.

words.tr: adj. 不名誉的；不光彩的；可耻的
words.ex: His actions were deemed dishonourable by the community.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为被社区认为是不名誉的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as dishonourable, you mean that it is shameful or disgraceful.

words.ex: She put the dirty plates into the dishwasher.
words.ex_cn: 她把脏盘子放进洗碗机里。
words.en: A dishwasher is a machine that washes dirty dishes automatically.

words.tr:
v. 使不再抱幻想；使理想破灭
n. 幻灭；理想破灭
words.ex: The bad experience disillusioned him about politics.
words.ex_cn: 这次糟糕的经历让他对政治不再抱幻想。
words.en: If a person or thing disillusions you, they make you realize that something is not as good as you thought it was.

words.tr: adj. 不再抱幻想的； v. “disillusion”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He became disillusioned after seeing the truth.
words.ex_cn: 在看到真相后，他不再抱幻想了。
words.en: If you are disillusioned with something, you are disappointed because it is not as good as you had expected.

words.ex: She disinfects the kitchen counter every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天给厨房台面消毒。
words.en: To disinfect something means to clean it using a substance that kills bacteria and germs.

words.ex: He uses disinfectant to clean the bathroom.
words.ex_cn: 他用消毒剂清洁浴室。
words.en: A disinfectant is a chemical substance that is used to kill harmful bacteria and viruses.

words.ex: The old bridge will disintegrate if no one fixes it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没人修理，这座旧桥会瓦解。
words.en: If something disintegrates, it breaks into many small pieces or parts and is destroyed.

words.ex: The old bridge began disintegration after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥在风暴后开始崩解。
words.en: The process of breaking into small parts or pieces and losing strength or effectiveness.

words.tr: adj. 不忠的；背叛的；不忠诚的
words.ex: He was disloyal to his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友不忠。
words.en: If someone is disloyal, they are not loyal to a person, organization, or idea that they are supposed to support.

words.ex: He felt dismay when he saw the low grade.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到低分时，感到沮丧。
words.en: Dismay is a feeling of unhappiness and disappointment.

words.ex: He dismissed her advice and walked away.
words.ex_cn: 他不理会她的建议，走开了。
words.en: If you dismiss someone, you send them away or allow them to leave.

words.ex: His dismissal made him very sad.
words.ex_cn: 他的被解雇让他非常难过。
words.en: The act of officially removing someone from their job, or the act of sending someone away or allowing them to leave.

words.tr: n. 不服从；不顺从；违抗
words.ex: The child showed disobedience by not doing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 孩子因为没做作业而表现出不服从。
words.en: The act of refusing to obey rules, laws, or someone in authority.

words.tr:
v. 派遣；调遣；发送
n. 快信；发送；派遣
words.ex: He will dispatch the package tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会寄出这个包裹。
words.en: To send someone or something to a particular place for a particular purpose.

words.tr: n. （学校、兵营或工厂的）医务室；药房
words.ex: The workers go to the dispensary when they feel sick.
words.ex_cn: 工人感到不舒服时去医务室。
words.en: A dispensary is a place where medicines are prepared and given out, especially in a hospital or clinic.

words.ex: The nurse will dispense medicine to the patients.
words.ex_cn: 护士将分发药品给病人。
words.en: To dispense means to distribute or provide something, especially in a systematic way, or to prepare and give out medicine.

words.ex: The police dispersed the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 警察驱散了人群。
words.en: If a crowd of people disperses or is dispersed, it breaks up and the people go in different directions.

words.ex: The displacement of the car was 10 meters east.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的位移是向东10米。
words.en: The act of moving something from its place or position, or the condition of having been moved from it.

words.tr: v. 使恼怒；使生气；使不悦
words.ex: The loud noise displeases her.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的声音让她不高兴。
words.en: If something or someone displeases you, they make you feel annoyed or angry.

words.ex: He showed his displeasure by staying silent.
words.ex_cn: 他通过保持沉默表现出不快。
words.en: Displeasure is the feeling of being annoyed or dissatisfied with someone or something.

words.ex: He used a disposable cup for his coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一次性杯子喝咖啡。
words.en: Something that is disposable is intended to be thrown away after use.

words.ex: The disposal of waste is important for the environment.
words.ex_cn: 废物的处理对环境很重要。
words.en: The act or process of getting rid of something, especially by throwing it away or selling it.

words.ex: His disposition is calm and kind.
words.ex_cn: 他的性情平静而善良。
words.en: Someone's disposition is the way that they tend to behave or feel.

words.tr:
n. 纠纷；争端；
v. 对（某事）有异议；
words.ex: The dispute between the two neighbors was about the fence.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间的纠纷是关于篱笆的。
words.en: A dispute is a disagreement or argument about something important.

words.tr: v. 使不合格；剥夺资格
words.ex: He was disqualified for breaking the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他因为违反规则而被取消资格。
words.en: If someone is disqualified from something, they are officially stopped from doing it, usually because they have done something wrong or broken a rule.

words.tr:
n. 漠视；忽视；
v. 漠视；不理会；不顾；
words.ex: His advice was met with disregard.
words.ex_cn: 他的建议遭到了漠视。
words.en: If you disregard something, you ignore it or do not take account of it.

words.tr: n. 不满；令人不满的事物；
words.ex: He showed dissatisfaction with the new rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定表示不满。
words.en: Dissatisfaction is a feeling of not being satisfied or pleased with something.

words.tr: v. 使不满意；使不满足；使失望
words.ex: The slow service dissatisfy the customers.
words.ex_cn: 缓慢的服务使顾客不满意。
words.en: If something dissatisfies you, it does not satisfy you or give you pleasure.

words.ex: The teacher asked us to dissect the poem line by line.
words.ex_cn: 老师让我们逐行仔细分析这首诗。
words.en: To dissect something means to cut it into pieces in order to examine its structure, or to study something in great detail.

words.ex: He expressed dissent about the new rule.
words.ex_cn: 他对新规定提出了异议。
words.en: Dissent is strong disagreement or dissatisfaction with a decision or opinion, especially one that is supported by most people or by people in authority.

words.ex: He wrote his dissertation on climate change.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一篇关于气候变化的学位论文。
words.en: A dissertation is a long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree.

words.tr:
adj. 持不同意见的
n. 意见不同的人；持不同政见者
words.ex: The dissident spoke out against the government.
words.ex_cn: 这位持不同政见者公开反对政府。
words.en: A dissident is a person who opposes official policy, especially that of an authoritarian state.

words.tr: adj. 不相似的；不一样的；不同的
words.ex: The two apples are dissimilar in color.
words.ex_cn: 这两个苹果颜色不同。
words.en: If one thing is dissimilar to another, or if two things are dissimilar, they are very different from each other.

words.tr: n. 分解；分裂；溶解；解体；解除；死亡
words.ex: The dissolution of sugar in water is quick.
words.ex_cn: 糖在水中的分解很快。
words.en: The act or process of ending or breaking up an organization, agreement, or legal arrangement.

words.ex: Sugar dissolves in water.
words.ex_cn: 糖在水中溶解。
words.en: If a substance dissolves in liquid or if you dissolve a substance, it becomes mixed with the liquid and disappears.

words.tr: v. 蒸馏；用蒸馏法提取；蒸馏出；提炼
words.ex: They distill water to remove impurities.
words.ex_cn: 他们通过蒸馏去除水中的杂质。
words.en: To distill a liquid means to purify it by heating it until it becomes a gas and then cooling it so that it becomes a liquid again. This process can also be used to extract the essential elements or meanings from something.

words.ex: The distillation of water removes impurities.
words.ex_cn: 水的蒸馏过程可以去除杂质。
words.en: The process of purifying a liquid by heating it until it becomes a vapor and then cooling the vapor to collect the purified liquid.

words.ex: This painting has a distinctive style.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画有独特的风格。
words.en: Something that is distinctive has a special quality or feature which makes it easily recognizable and different from other things of the same type.

words.tr: adj. 可区别的；可辨别的
words.ex: The two colors are distinguishable under bright light.
words.ex_cn: 在强光下，这两种颜色是可以区分的。
words.en: If something is distinguishable, it can be recognized or identified as different from something else.

words.tr: v. 区分；“distinguish”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 卓越的；著名的；
words.ex: He distinguished the fake coin from the real one.
words.ex_cn: 他把假硬币和真硬币区分开来。
words.en: If you describe a person or their work as distinguished, you mean that they have been very successful in their career and have a good reputation.

words.ex: The mirror distorts my face.
words.ex_cn: 这面镜子扭曲了我的脸。
words.en: If you distort a statement, fact, or idea, you report or represent it in an untrue way.

words.ex: The loud music distract me from my homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我无法专心做作业。
words.en: If something distracts you or your attention, it makes you stop concentrating on what you are doing.

words.ex: The loud music was a distraction while I tried to study.
words.ex_cn: 当我试图学习时，大声的音乐让我分心。
words.en: Something that makes it difficult for you to concentrate on what you are doing.

words.ex: He felt great distress when he lost his job.
words.ex_cn: 当他失去工作时，他感到非常忧虑。
words.en: Distress is a feeling of extreme worry, sadness, or pain.

words.tr:
n. 怀疑；不信任
v. 怀疑；不信任
words.ex: He feels distrust toward strangers.
words.ex_cn: 他不信任陌生人。
words.en: If you distrust someone or something, you think they are not honest, reliable, or safe.

words.ex: The company plans to diversify its products.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划使产品多样化。
words.en: To diversify means to make or become more varied or different. It often refers to the process of a company or individual expanding their range of products or activities to reduce risk or to explore new opportunities.

words.ex: The loud music was a diversion from his worries.
words.ex_cn: 那嘈杂的音乐分散了他对烦恼的注意力。
words.en: A diversion is an action or event that attracts your attention away from what you are doing or should be doing.

words.ex: The road was diverted around the park.
words.ex_cn: 这条路被改道绕过公园。
words.en: If you divert someone or something, you cause them to change direction or to go somewhere different.

words.tr: adj. 可被整除的；可分的
words.ex: The number 12 is divisible by 3.
words.ex_cn: 12 能被 3 整除。
words.en: Capable of being divided, especially with no remainder.

words.tr: adj. 头晕目眩的；头昏眼花的；
words.ex: He felt dizzy after spinning around quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他快速转圈后感到头晕目眩。
words.en: If you feel dizzy, you feel that you are losing your balance and are about to fall.

words.ex: The dockyard was bustling with activity as ships were being repaired and built.
words.ex_cn: 造船厂里忙碌非凡，船只正在被修理和建造。
words.en: A dockyard is a place where ships are built or repaired.

words.ex: The church teaches its doctrine to all members.
words.ex_cn: 教会向所有成员传授它的教义。
words.en: A doctrine is a set of beliefs or principles that are taught or accepted by a particular group, especially in religion or politics.

words.tr:
n. 纪录片；
adj. 文书的；
words.ex: We watched a documentary about pandas last night.
words.ex_cn: 我们昨晚看了一部关于熊猫的纪录片。
words.en: A documentary is a film or television or radio programme that gives factual information about a particular subject.

words.tr:
v. 避开；躲避
n. 躲避；诡计
words.ex: He dodged the ball quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他迅速躲开了球。
words.en: If you dodge, you move quickly, often to avoid being hit, caught, or seen.

words.tr: v. 缠住；“dog”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The reporter dogged the politician everywhere.
words.ex_cn: 记者紧紧跟随这位政治家到处。
words.en: If you describe someone's actions as dogged, you mean that they are determined to continue with something even if it becomes difficult or dangerous.

words.ex: The dolphin jumped high out of the water.
words.ex_cn: 海豚从水中高高跳起。
words.en: A dolphin is a marine mammal that is known for its intelligence and friendly nature towards humans.

words.ex: The church has a big dome above the altar.
words.ex_cn: 教堂的祭坛上方有一个大穹顶。
words.en: A dome is a rounded vault made of either curved segments or a shell of revolution, meaning an arch rotated around its central vertical axis.

words.tr: adj. 家庭的；国内的；驯养的；
words.ex: She prefers domestic chores over going out.
words.ex_cn: 她更喜欢做家务而不是外出。
words.en: Domestic means relating to the home, family, or household affairs. It can also refer to something that is made or produced within a country and not imported.

words.tr: n. 支配；领土；统治（权）；管辖
words.ex: The king had dominion over the land.
words.ex_cn: 国王对这片土地拥有统治权。
words.en: Dominion refers to the power or right of governing and controlling; it can also denote a territory or sphere of influence.

words.ex: He knocked down the domino with a finger.
words.ex_cn: 他用一根手指推倒了多米诺骨牌。
words.en: A domino is a small, flat, rectangular block used as a gaming object. Dominoes are typically made of bone, wood, or plastic and are used in various games.

words.tr: v. 完成；“do”的过去分词； adj. 已完成的；
words.ex: I done my homework.
words.ex_cn: 我完成了我的作业。
words.en: If something is done, it has been completed or finished.

words.ex: The donor gave money to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 捐赠者向医院捐了钱。
words.en: A donor is a person or organization that gives something, especially money, to a charity or other organization.

words.ex: He ate a donut for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃了一个甜甜圈。
words.en: A donut is a small, circular cake, typically with a hole in the center, fried and often covered with sugar or icing.

words.tr:
n. 厄运；毁灭；死亡
v. 注定；判决
words.ex: The old prophecy spoke of doom for the kingdom.
words.ex_cn: 古老的预言说这个王国将遭遇厄运。
words.en: Doom is a terrible fate or destiny that you cannot avoid, especially death or destruction.

words.ex: The package arrived at my doorstep.
words.ex_cn: 包裹送到我家门口了。
words.en: A doorstep is a step in front of an outer door to a building.

words.ex: The cat sat in the doorway.
words.ex_cn: 猫坐在门口。
words.en: A doorway is the space in a wall where a door opens and closes, or the covered area just outside a door.

words.ex: He lives in the dorm with three roommates.
words.ex_cn: 他和三个室友住在宿舍里。
words.en: A dorm is a large building at a college or university where students live.

words.ex: He lives in the dormitory with three roommates.
words.ex_cn: 他和三个室友住在宿舍里。
words.en: A dormitory is a large bedroom where many people sleep, especially in a school or college.

words.ex: The doctor gave him a small dose of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 医生给了他一小剂量的药。
words.en: A dose of a medicine or a drug is the amount of it that you take at one time, or the amount that is recommended for you to take.

words.ex: He drew a dot on the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他在纸上画了一个小圆点。
words.en: A dot is a very small round mark, for example one that is used as the top part of the letter 'i', as a full stop, or as a decimal point.

words.ex: He is doubtless the best player on the team.
words.ex_cn: 他无疑是队里最好的球员。
words.en: used to say that something is almost certain or very likely

words.ex: The downcast eyes of the boy showed he was sad.
words.ex_cn: 男孩低垂的眼睛显示出他很难过。
words.en: If you are downcast, you are feeling sad and without hope.

words.ex: The king's greed led to his downfall.
words.ex_cn: 国王的贪婪导致了他的没落。
words.en: The collapse of a person or organization's power, status, or success.

words.ex: The downpour soaked everyone outside.
words.ex_cn: 暴雨把外面的每个人都淋湿了。
words.en: A downpour is a sudden and unexpected heavy fall of rain.

words.tr:
adv. 向下地；
adj. 向下的；
words.ex: The leaves fell downward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 树叶慢慢向下飘落。
words.en: Moving or leading towards a lower place or level

words.ex: The dragonfly flies fast over the pond.
words.ex_cn: 蜻蜓在池塘上快速飞行。
words.en: A dragonfly is an insect with a long, thin body and two pairs of transparent wings. Dragonflies are often seen near water.

words.ex: The city improved its drainage system after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 洪水之后，这座城市改进了它的排水系统。
words.en: Drainage is the system or process by which water or other liquids are drained from a place.

words.ex: He is a famous dramatist who writes plays.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位著名的剧作家，写剧本。
words.en: A dramatist is a person who writes plays.

words.tr: v. 改编为戏剧；渲染；使戏剧化
words.ex: They dramatize the novel for the stage.
words.ex_cn: 他们将这部小说改编成舞台剧。
words.en: If a book or story is dramatized, it is written or presented as a play, film, or television drama.

words.ex: The company made drastic cuts to save money.
words.ex_cn: 公司进行了急剧的削减以节省资金。
words.en: If you describe a change or action as drastic, you mean that it is extreme and often severe.

words.ex: The drawback of this phone is its short battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的缺点是电池续航时间短。
words.en: A drawback is a feature of something that makes it less useful or desirable than it could be.

words.tr: phrase. 浴袍；晨衣（指在家穿着的宽松长袍）
words.ex: He put on his dressing gown after waking up.
words.ex_cn: 他醒来后穿上了他的晨袍。
words.en: A dressing gown is a long, loose robe which you wear over your night clothes when you are not in bed.

words.tr:
v. 下毛毛雨；（毛毛雨似的）洒落
n. 毛毛细雨
words.ex: It is drizzling outside.
words.ex_cn: 外面正在下毛毛雨。
words.en: Light rain falling in very fine drops.

words.tr:
n. 低垂；凋萎；萎靡
v. 低垂；凋萎；萎靡
words.ex: The flowers droop in the hot sun.
words.ex_cn: 花朵在烈日下低垂。
words.en: If something droops, it hangs or leans downwards with no strength or firmness.

words.ex: The heavy rain drowned the small village.
words.ex_cn: 大雨淹没了这个小村庄。
words.en: To die by being underwater too long and unable to breathe, or to kill someone in this way.

words.ex: The druggist dispensed the prescribed medication.
words.ex_cn: 药剂师配发了处方药物。
words.en: A druggist is a person who is qualified to prepare and dispense drugs and medicines, or a person who owns or runs a drugstore.

words.ex: He bought medicine at the drugstore.
words.ex_cn: 他在药店买了药。
words.en: A drugstore is a shop where medicines and other small items are sold.

words.ex: He is a drummer in a rock band.
words.ex_cn: 他是摇滚乐队的一名鼓手。
words.en: A drummer is a person who plays a drum or drums.

words.tr: n. 鼓槌；（煮熟的）家禽的腿下部
words.ex: He picked up the drumstick and hit the drum.
words.ex_cn: 他拿起鼓槌敲了鼓。
words.en: A drumstick is a stick used for playing a drum, or the lower part of a chicken's or other bird's leg, which is cooked and eaten.

words.tr: n. 烘干机； adj. “dry”的比较级；
words.ex: I put my clothes in the dryer after washing.
words.ex_cn: 我洗完衣服后把它们放进烘干机。
words.en: A dryer is a machine that dries things, especially clothes, by using hot air.

words.ex: He has a dual role as teacher and coach.
words.ex_cn: 他同时担任老师和教练的双重角色。
words.en: Having two parts or aspects.

words.tr: adj. 可疑的；怀疑的；拿不准的；
words.ex: The deal seemed dubious to me.
words.ex_cn: 这个交易在我看来很可疑。
words.en: If you describe something as dubious, you mean that you do not consider it to be completely honest, safe, or reliable.

words.ex: The duchess walks in the garden every morning.
words.ex_cn: 公爵夫人每天早上都在花园里散步。
words.en: A duchess is the wife or widow of a duke, or a woman who holds the rank of duke in her own right.

words.ex: The duckling swims behind its mother.
words.ex_cn: 小鸭子跟在妈妈后面游泳。
words.en: A duckling is a young duck.

words.ex: The duke lives in a big castle.
words.ex_cn: 公爵住在一座大城堡里。
words.en: A duke is a male ruler of a small independent state, or a man of very high rank in the British nobility.

words.ex: He duly submitted his homework on time.
words.ex_cn: 他适时地按时交了作业。
words.en: If something is duly done, it is done in the correct way or at the correct time; properly.

words.tr:
n. 动物的粪便
v. 施粪肥于
words.ex: The cow left dung on the grass.
words.ex_cn: 牛在草地上留下了粪便。
words.en: Dung is the excrement of animals, used as manure.

words.tr: v. 复制；复印；再做一次；
words.ex: He duplicated the file to save a copy.
words.ex_cn: 他复制了该文件以保存一份副本。
words.en: To duplicate something means to make an exact copy of it.

words.ex: This bag is durable and lasts for years.
words.ex_cn: 这个包很耐用，可以用很多年。
words.en: Something that is durable is strong and lasts a long time without breaking or becoming weaker.

words.ex: The birds flew home at dusk.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在黄昏时飞回家。
words.en: Dusk is the time just before night when the daylight has almost gone but when it is not completely dark.

words.ex: He threw the trash into the dustbin.
words.ex_cn: 他把垃圾扔进了垃圾桶。
words.en: A dustbin is a container for waste, especially one that is kept outside a house or other building.

words.ex: She picked up a duster and started cleaning the shelves.
words.ex_cn: 她拿起一块抹布开始清理架子。
words.en: A duster is a cloth or brush that you use to remove dust from furniture, or a person whose job is to remove dust from places.

words.ex: The dustman collects trash every morning.
words.ex_cn: 垃圾清运工每天早上收集垃圾。
words.en: A dustman is a person whose job is to remove waste from outside houses and other buildings.

words.ex: She picked up the crumbs with a dustpan and brush.
words.ex_cn: 她用簸箕和刷子捡起了碎屑。
words.en: A dustpan is a flat container with a handle into which you brush dust and dirt.

words.ex: The fairy tale features a dwarf who lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这个童话故事中有一个住在小房子里的侏儒。
