words.ex: The inclusion of all students is important.
words.ex_cn: 包含所有学生是很重要的。
words.en: The act of including or the state of being included.

words.tr: adj. 无能力的；不称职的；不能胜任的；
words.ex: He is incompetent at managing simple tasks.
words.ex_cn: 他无法胜任简单的任务。
words.en: If you describe someone as incompetent, you are criticizing them because they are unable to do their job or a task properly.

words.tr: adj. 不能理解的；费解的
words.ex: The instructions were incomprehensible.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明让人完全看不懂。
words.en: If something is incomprehensible, you cannot understand it because it is so complex or unusual.

words.ex: His answers were inconsistent.
words.ex_cn: 他的答案不一致。
words.en: If you describe someone as inconsistent, you are criticizing them for not behaving in the same way every time a similar situation occurs.

words.tr: adj. 引起麻烦的；不方便的；
words.ex: The late bus is inconvenient for me.
words.ex_cn: 这趟晚班公交车让我很麻烦。
words.en: If something is inconvenient, it causes problems or difficulties for you.

words.ex: The new plan incorporates feedback from students.
words.ex_cn: 新计划包含了学生的反馈。
words.en: If one thing incorporates another thing, it includes the other thing.

words.ex: The movie was incredible.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影太棒了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as incredible, you like them very much or are impressed by them, because they are extremely or unusually good.

words.tr:
adj. 不能治愈的；无可救药的
n. 患不治之症者；不能治愈的人
words.ex: The disease is incurable.
words.ex_cn: 这种病无法治愈。
words.en: If someone has an incurable disease, they cannot be cured of it.

words.ex: He is indebted to the bank for a large loan.
words.ex_cn: 他欠银行一大笔贷款。
words.en: If you say that you are indebted to someone for something, you mean that you are very grateful to them for something.

words.tr: adj. 与好的品味相悖的；不合礼节的；下流的；有伤风化的
words.ex: He wore an indecent shirt to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一件不雅的衬衫去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as indecent, you mean that it is shocking or offensive, usually because it relates to sex or nakedness.

words.tr: adj. 站不住脚的；不可辩解的；不能防卫的
words.ex: His excuse was indefensible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口是无法辩护的。
words.en: If you say that something is indefensible, you mean that it cannot be justified or supported because it is completely wrong or unacceptable.

words.tr: adj. 难下定义的；难以说明的；不确定的
words.ex: Her joy was indefinable.
words.ex_cn: 她的快乐无法形容。
words.en: If you describe something as indefinable, you mean that it is difficult to explain or describe because it is unusual or complicated.

words.tr: adj. 模糊的；不确定的；无限期的
words.ex: He gave an indefinite answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个不确定的答案。
words.en: If you describe something as indefinite, you mean that it has not been decided or defined clearly, or that it has no clear limit or end.

words.ex: He showed indifference to his friend's problems.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的问题表现出冷淡。
words.en: Indifference is the state of being indifferent, especially in the sense of not caring or being uninterested.

words.ex: He felt indignant when they blamed him for the mistake.
words.ex_cn: 当他们把错误归咎于他时，他感到愤愤不平。
words.en: If you are indignant, you are shocked and angry, because you think that something is unjust or unfair.

words.ex: He felt indignation when he saw the unfair rule.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到不公平的规则时，他感到愤怒。
words.en: Indignation is a feeling of anger and surprise which you have when you think that something is wrong or unfair.

words.ex: He suffered an indignity at the hands of the guards.
words.ex_cn: 他受到了守卫的羞辱。
words.en: An indignity is a situation or event that causes you to feel ashamed or embarrassed because it involves something that is unfair or insulting.

words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.ex: He values individualism in his work.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中重视个人主义。
words.en: Individualism is the belief that the rights and freedom of the individual are the most important rights in a society.

words.ex: The ad induced him to buy the product.
words.ex_cn: 这则广告诱使他购买了该产品。
words.en: To induce a state or condition means to cause it.

words.ex: He accepted the job because of the financial inducement.
words.ex_cn: 他因为经济诱因接受了这份工作。
words.en: Something that is offered to someone to persuade them to do something.

words.tr: n. 工业家；实业家；企业家
words.ex: The industrialist built a large factory in the town.
words.ex_cn: 这位工业家在镇上建了一家大工厂。
words.en: An industrialist is a person who owns or is involved in the management of an industrial enterprise.

words.ex: The country wants to industrialize quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家想快速工业化。
words.en: To industrialize means to develop industry in a country or region on a wide scale.

words.ex: He is an industrious student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤勉的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is industrious works hard and is determined.

words.tr: adj. 无效果的；不起作用的；不奏效的；
words.ex: The medicine was ineffective against the cold.
words.ex_cn: 这种药对感冒无效。
words.en: If someone or something is ineffective, they do not achieve the intended result.

words.ex: The old machine is inefficient and uses too much energy.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器效率低，耗能太多。
words.en: If someone or something is inefficient, they do not use time, energy, or resources in the best way.

words.ex: The inequality between rich and poor is growing.
words.ex_cn: 贫富之间的不平等正在加剧。
words.en: Inequality refers to the unfair situation in society when some people have more opportunities, money, etc. than other people.

words.ex: The inert gas does not react with other elements.
words.ex_cn: 这种惰性气体不与其他元素发生反应。
words.en: If someone or something is inert, they are not moving or reacting in any way.

words.ex: The ball keeps moving because of inertia.
words.ex_cn: 球因为惯性继续移动。
words.en: Inertia is the tendency of a physical object to continue moving in a straight line at a constant speed, or to stay at rest, unless it is acted upon by a force.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.tr: adj. 不精确的；不准确的
words.ex: The answer is inexact because we used rough measurements.
words.ex_cn: 答案不精确，因为我们使用了粗略的测量。
words.en: If something is inexact, it is not precise or accurate.

words.ex: The child showed signs of talent in infancy.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在婴儿期就表现出天赋。
words.en: The earliest period of childhood, especially before the ability to walk has been acquired.

words.ex: From the clues, he made a logical inference.
words.ex_cn: 从线索中，他做出了一个合理的推论。
words.en: An inference is a conclusion that you draw about something by using information that you already have about it.

words.ex: This product is inferior to the other one.
words.ex_cn: 这个产品比另一个差。
words.en: If one person or thing is inferior to another, they are not as good, important, or valuable as the other person or thing.

words.ex: The soil is too infertile to grow crops.
words.ex_cn: 这片土地太贫瘠了，无法种植庄稼。
words.en: Infertile land or soil is not able to produce good crops or plants. An infertile person, animal, or plant cannot have babies, eggs, or seeds.

words.tr:
n. （动词）不定式
adj. 不定式的
words.ex: The infinitive of 'run' is 'to run'.
words.ex_cn: “run”的不定式是“to run”。
words.en: The basic form of a verb, without an inflection binding it to a particular subject or tense.

words.ex: The stars seem to go on to infinity.
words.ex_cn: 星星似乎延伸到无限。
words.en: Infinity is a concept of something that is unlimited, endless, without bound.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.ex: The price of bread went up because of inflation.
words.ex_cn: 由于通货膨胀，面包的价格上涨了。
words.en: Inflation is a general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.

words.ex: He is an influential teacher in our school.
words.ex_cn: 他是我们学校一位有影响力的老师。
words.en: Having great influence on someone or something.

words.ex: He caught influenza last winter.
words.ex_cn: 他去年冬天得了流感。
words.en: Influenza is an infectious disease caused by the influenza virus, characterized by fever, sore throat, muscle pain, severe headache, coughing, and weakness.

words.ex: The police relied on an informant to find the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察依靠一名信息提供人找到了小偷。
words.en: An informant is someone who gives information to another person or organization, especially information that is secret or private.

words.tr: adj. 了解情况的； v. 通知；告知；“inform”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is an informed voter who reads the news daily.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个了解情况的选民，每天阅读新闻。
words.en: If someone is informed, they know a lot about a particular subject or situation.

words.tr: n. 告密者；告发者；线人
words.ex: The informer told the police about the crime.
words.ex_cn: 举报人向警方透露了这起犯罪。
words.en: An informer is someone who gives information to the police or other authorities about criminal activities.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.ex: His ingenuity solved the problem with a simple tool.
words.ex_cn: 他的独创力用一个简单的工具解决了问题。
words.en: Ingenuity is the ability to think of clever and original ways to solve problems.

words.ex: Sugar is an ingredient in this cake.
words.ex_cn: 糖是这个蛋糕的一个成分。
words.en: An ingredient is one of the substances that are combined to make something, especially in cooking.

words.ex: Birds inhabit the forest near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类居住在湖边的森林里。
words.en: If a place or region is inhabited by a group of people or a species of animal, those people or animals live there.

words.tr: adj. 适于居住的；可居住的
words.ex: The planet is not inhabitable because it is too hot.
words.ex_cn: 这颗行星不适合居住，因为它太热了。
words.en: Capable of being lived in; suitable for living in.

words.ex: The inhabitant lives in a small house.
words.ex_cn: 这位居民住在一所小房子里。
words.en: An inhabitant of a place is one of the people who live there.

words.ex: He inhale the fresh air in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 他早上吸入新鲜空气。
words.en: To inhale means to breathe in air, smoke, or gas.

words.ex: Honesty is an inherent quality of a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是好领导固有的品质。
words.en: Existing in something as a permanent, essential, or characteristic attribute.

words.ex: He inherited a house from his father.
words.ex_cn: 他从父亲那里继承了一所房子。
words.en: If you inherit something such as a trait, characteristic, or quality, you are born with it, because your parents or ancestors had it. If you inherit money or property, you receive it from someone who has died.

words.tr: adj. 野蛮的；无人性的；残忍的
words.ex: The prison conditions were inhuman.
words.ex_cn: 监狱的条件十分野蛮。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as inhuman, you mean that they are extremely cruel or unpleasant.

words.ex: The prison conditions were inhumane.
words.ex_cn: 监狱的条件是不人道的。
words.en: If you describe something as inhumane, you mean that it is extremely cruel.

words.ex: The war showed the inhumanity of violence.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争展现了暴力的非人性。
words.en: The quality of lacking compassion or kindness; cruelty.

words.tr: adj. 无法仿效的；不可比拟的
words.ex: Her inimitable style of writing has captured the hearts of many readers.
words.ex_cn: 她那独特的写作风格赢得了许多读者的心。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as inimitable, you mean that they are so good or unusual that it is unlikely that anyone or anything else could be like them.

words.ex: He will initiate a new project next week.
words.ex_cn: 他将在下周发起一个新项目。
words.en: To initiate something means to start it or cause it to happen.

words.ex: The doctor gave him an injection for the pain.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他打了一针来缓解疼痛。
words.en: An injection is the act of putting a liquid, especially a drug, into a person's body using a needle and a syringe.

words.tr: n. 非正义；不公平；不公正
words.ex: He cried out against the injustice.
words.ex_cn: 他抗议这种不公。
words.en: Injustice refers to the lack of fairness or justice in a situation or action.

words.ex: I went to dinner with my in-laws last night.
words.ex_cn: 我昨晚和我的亲家一起吃了晚饭。
words.en: Your in-laws are the parents and close relatives of your husband or wife.

words.ex: The small boat docked at the inlet.
words.ex_cn: 小船停靠在小水湾。
words.en: An inlet is a narrow strip of water that leads from a sea or lake into the land or between islands.

words.tr: n. 客栈老板；旅店老板
words.ex: The innkeeper served tea to the travelers.
words.ex_cn: 旅店老板给旅客们端上了茶。
words.en: An innkeeper is a person who owns or manages an inn.

words.tr: adj. 天真无邪的；无辜的；
words.ex: The innocent child smiled at the stranger.
words.ex_cn: 那个天真无邪的孩子对陌生人笑了。
words.en: If someone is innocent, they did not commit a crime which they have been accused of.

words.ex: The company wants to innovate its production process.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司想改革它的生产流程。
words.en: To innovate means to introduce changes and new ideas in the way something is done or made.

words.ex: There are innumerable stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有数不清的星星。
words.en: Too many to be counted; very many.

words.tr:
n. 输入；
v. 输入；
words.ex: The computer needs user input to work.
words.ex_cn: 计算机需要用户输入才能工作。
words.en: Input is information that is put into a system or machine so that it can operate.

words.ex: The court held an inquest into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 法院对这起事故进行了审讯。
words.en: An inquest is an official investigation to discover the cause of something, especially a death.

words.ex: He is inquiring about the train schedule.
words.ex_cn: 他正在询问火车时刻表。
words.en: If someone has an inquiring mind, they are interested in learning about many different things.

words.ex: The police opened an inquiry into the accident.
words.ex_cn: 警方对这起事故展开了调查。
words.en: An inquiry is a question which you ask in order to get some information.

words.tr: adj. 疯狂的；精神失常的；精神错乱的
words.ex: He thinks it's insane to drive without a license.
words.ex_cn: 他认为无证驾驶是疯狂的。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as insane, you mean that they are very foolish or crazy.

words.ex: He inscribes his name on the stone.
words.ex_cn: 他把名字刻在石头上。
words.en: To write, mark, or engrave (words, symbols, etc.) on a surface, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.ex: The ancient stone has an inscription in Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这块古老的石头上有一段拉丁文碑文。
words.en: An inscription is a piece of writing or a short message that is written or carved on something, especially as a formal or permanent record.

words.ex: Farmers use insecticide to kill bugs on crops.
words.ex_cn: 农民使用杀虫剂来杀死作物上的害虫。
words.en: A substance used for killing insects.

words.tr: n. 没有知觉；不在乎；不关心
words.ex: He showed insensibility to the pain.
words.ex_cn: 他对疼痛毫无感觉。
words.en: The condition of being unable to feel or perceive; lack of sensation or consciousness.

words.tr: adj. 分不开的；形影不离的
words.ex: They are inseparable friends.
words.ex_cn: 他们是形影不离的朋友。
words.en: If two or more people are inseparable, they are such good friends that they spend most of their time together.

words.tr: adj. 无关紧要的；不重要的；
words.ex: The mistake was insignificant and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误无关紧要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as insignificant, you mean that they are small or unimportant, and therefore not worth considering seriously.

words.ex: His smile seemed insincere.
words.ex_cn: 他的微笑显得不真心。
words.en: If you say that someone is insincere, you are being critical of them because they say things they do not really mean, usually pleasant, admiring, or encouraging things.

words.tr: adj. 坚持的；迫切要求的；持续的
words.ex: He is insistent about finishing his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他坚持要完成作业。
words.en: If someone is insistent, they keep demanding something and refuse to accept any opposition or excuses.

words.ex: The teacher will inspect our homework tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天会检查我们的作业。
words.en: If you inspect something, you look at it very carefully, usually in order to find out something about it.

words.tr: n. 检查；视察；查看；审视；
words.ex: The teacher did an inspection of the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 老师对教室进行了检查。
words.en: An inspection is an official visit to a building or organization to check that everything is satisfactory and that rules are being obeyed.

words.tr: n. 检查员；巡视员；视察员；
words.ex: The inspector checked the building for safety.
words.ex_cn: 检查员检查了建筑物的安全性。
words.en: An inspector is a person whose job is to inspect something.

words.ex: He will install the new software on his computer.
words.ex_cn: 他将在他的电脑上安装新软件。
words.en: To set up or fix in position for use or service.

words.ex: The installation of the new machine took two days.
words.ex_cn: 新机器的安置花了两天时间。
words.en: The act of installing or the state of being installed.

words.ex: He paid the first installment last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周支付了第一期分期付款。
words.en: An installment is one of the amounts, usually equal, into which a debt is divided for payment at stated intervals over a fixed period.

words.ex: Birds fly south by instinct.
words.ex_cn: 鸟类凭本能飞向南方。
words.en: An instinct is the natural tendency that a person or animal has to behave or react in a particular way.

words.ex: The hospital is an institutional building.
words.ex_cn: 这家医院是一座大型机构的建筑。
words.en: Relating to or characteristic of an institution, especially a large organization or public body.

words.ex: The teacher instructed the students to open their books.
words.ex_cn: 老师指示学生打开书。
words.en: To instruct someone means to tell or teach them to do something, especially in a formal or official way.

words.tr: adj. 教育性的；有启发的；有益的
words.ex: The movie is instructive for children.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影对孩子们很有教育意义。
words.en: Providing useful or interesting information or knowledge.

words.ex: The instructor explained the math problem clearly.
words.ex_cn: 教员清楚地讲解了这道数学题。
words.en: An instructor is someone who teaches a skill or subject, especially in a college or university, or in a specialized field such as driving or skiing.

words.tr: adj. 有帮助的；乐器的；仪器的；
words.ex: Her advice was instrumental in helping me pass the exam.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对帮助我通过考试很有帮助。
words.en: If someone or something is instrumental in a process, plan, or system, they are one of the most important influences in causing it to happen.

words.ex: The water supply is insufficient for the whole village.
words.ex_cn: 供水对整个村庄来说是不充分的。
words.en: If something is insufficient, it is not enough for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The house has good insulation to keep warm in winter.
words.ex_cn: 这所房子有良好的绝缘层以在冬天保暖。
words.en: Insulation is a material or substance that is used to stop heat, electricity, or sound from going from one place to another.

words.tr: n. 隔热（或绝缘、隔音等的）材料（或装置）；
words.ex: Glass is a good insulator for heat.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃是良好的隔热材料。
words.en: An insulator is a material or device that prevents or reduces the passage of heat, electricity, or sound.

words.tr: adj. 侮辱的； v. “insult”的现在分词；
words.ex: His insulting words made her cry.
words.ex_cn: 他侮辱的话让她哭了。
words.en: If you describe someone's remarks or actions as insulting, you mean they are rude and offensive.

words.tr: adj. 被保险的； v. 确保；“insure”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The insured car was repaired after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 这辆被保险的车在事故后得到了维修。
words.en: Covered by insurance; a person or entity whose life or property is covered by an insurance policy.

words.ex: The insurer paid for the car repair.
words.ex_cn: 保险公司支付了汽车修理费用。
words.en: An insurer is a company or person that provides insurance, which is a financial arrangement that provides compensation for loss, damage, illness, or death in return for payment of a specified premium.

words.ex: The vase remained intact after the fall.
words.ex_cn: 花瓶从高处摔下后依然完整无缺。
words.en: Something that is intact is complete and has not been damaged or changed.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.ex: His intellect helps him solve difficult problems.
words.ex_cn: 他的智力帮助他解决难题。
words.en: The ability to understand and think in a logical way about things.

words.ex: The storm will intensify tonight.
words.ex_cn: 风暴今晚会加强。
words.en: To make or become more intense or intensive.

words.tr:
n. 意图；目的；
adj. 专注的；
words.ex: His intent was to help, not to hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他的意图是帮助，而不是伤害。
words.en: If you are intent on doing something, you are determined to get it done. If you have an intent to do something, you have a plan or purpose in mind.

words.ex: The police intercepted the stolen car.
words.ex_cn: 警察拦截了那辆被盗的汽车。
words.en: If you intercept someone or something that is going from one place to another, you stop them before they get there.

words.ex: Her intercession helped to resolve the conflict.
words.ex_cn: 她的调解帮助解决了冲突。
words.en: Intercession is the act of intervening on behalf of another, especially in prayer.

words.ex: The two cultures have a lot of interchange.
words.ex_cn: 这两种文化有很多交流。
words.en: The act or process of exchanging things with each other, especially ideas or information.

words.tr: n. 内部通话系统（或设备）； 对讲机
words.ex: He pressed the intercom to ask for help.
words.ex_cn: 他按了对讲机来寻求帮助。
words.en: An intercom is a communication system that allows people in different parts of a building or vehicle to speak to each other.

words.tr: adj. 洲际的；洲与洲之间的
words.ex: He flew on an intercontinental flight to New York.
words.ex_cn: 他乘坐了一趟洲际航班前往纽约。
words.en: An intercontinental activity or service involves going from one continent to another.

words.ex: There is little intercourse between the two villages.
words.ex_cn: 这两个村庄之间很少交往。
words.en: Intercourse refers to communication or dealings between individuals or groups, or sexual activity between people.

words.ex: Countries rely on each other for trade and resources, showing interdependence.
words.ex_cn: 国家之间依靠彼此进行贸易和资源交换，体现了相互依赖。
words.en: A situation in which people or things depend on each other.

words.ex: The radio signal suffered from interference.
words.ex_cn: 收音机信号受到了干扰。
words.en: Interference refers to the action of interfering or the process of being interfered with, especially in a context where it is unwelcome or inappropriate.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.tr:
n. 内部；
adj. 内部的；
words.ex: The interior of the house is very cozy.
words.ex_cn: 房子的内部非常舒适。
words.en: The interior of something is the inside part of it.

words.ex: He is an intermediate student in English.
words.ex_cn: 他是英语的中级学生。
words.en: An intermediate stage, level, or position is one that occurs between two other stages, levels, or positions.

words.ex: The internal parts of the machine need repair.
words.ex_cn: 机器的内部零件需要修理。
words.en: Internal is used to describe things that exist or happen inside a particular person, object, or place.

words.ex: He interprets the poem as a love story.
words.ex_cn: 他把这首诗解释为一个爱情故事。
words.en: If you interpret something in a particular way, you decide that this is its meaning or significance.

words.ex: He is an interpreter for the United Nations.
words.ex_cn: 他是联合国的口译员。
words.en: An interpreter is a person whose job is to translate what someone is saying into another language, especially in a situation where people are speaking different languages.

words.ex: The two lines intersect at point A.
words.ex_cn: 两条线在点A相交。
words.en: If two or more lines or roads intersect, they meet or cross each other.

words.tr: n. 交叉；相交；十字路口；交叉路口；
words.ex: The intersection of two roads is busy.
words.ex_cn: 两条路的交叉口很繁忙。
words.en: An intersection is a place where roads or other lines meet or cross.

words.ex: There is a five-minute interval between the two classes.
words.ex_cn: 两节课之间有五分钟的间隔。
words.en: An interval is a period of time between two events or dates.

words.ex: The teacher intervened when the students argued.
words.ex_cn: 当学生们争吵时，老师进行了干涉。
words.en: If you intervene in a situation, you become involved in it and try to change it.

words.ex: The teacher made an intervention to help the student.
words.ex_cn: 老师进行了干预以帮助学生。
words.en: Intervention is the act of intervening, especially in a situation to prevent something undesirable from happening.

words.tr:
adj. 干涉主义的；进行干涉的
n. 干涉主义者；主张干预的人
words.ex: The government is interventionist in the economy.
words.ex_cn: 政府在经济中采取干预主义政策。
words.en: An interventionist is someone who believes in or practices intervention, especially in the affairs of another country.

words.tr: n. 被面试者；被采访者；
words.ex: The interviewee answered all the questions calmly.
words.ex_cn: 被面试者冷静地回答了所有问题。
words.en: A person who is interviewed.

words.ex: The intestine helps digest food.
words.ex_cn: 肠道帮助消化食物。
words.en: The part of the alimentary canal between the stomach and the anus.

words.ex: The noise was intolerable.
words.ex_cn: 这噪音无法忍受。
words.en: If you describe something as intolerable, you mean that it is so bad or extreme that no one can bear it or tolerate it.

words.ex: He is intolerant of people who are late.
words.ex_cn: 他不能容忍迟到的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as intolerant, you mean that they do not accept behavior and opinions that are different from their own.

words.ex: His intonation made the sentence sound friendly.
words.ex_cn: 他的语调让这句话听起来很友好。
words.en: Intonation is the way the voice rises and falls in speech, especially the pitch pattern in a sentence.

words.tr: adj. 引导的；介绍的；开端的；
words.ex: This is an introductory book for beginners.
words.ex_cn: 这是一本为初学者引导的书。
words.en: An introductory remark, event, or action is one that comes at the beginning of something, often in order to explain or introduce it.

words.ex: The intruder broke into the house at night.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者在晚上闯入了房子。
words.en: An intruder is a person who enters a place or situation where they are not wanted.

words.ex: The invader came from a faraway land.
words.ex_cn: 入侵者来自一个遥远的地方。
words.en: An invader is someone who enters a place by force in order to conquer or occupy it.

words.ex: The ticket is invalid because it expired.
words.ex_cn: 这张票无效，因为它已经过期了。
words.en: If something is invalid, it is not legally or officially acceptable, or it is not based on truth or reason.

words.tr: adj. 无价的；非常宝贵的；
words.ex: Her advice was invaluable to me.
words.ex_cn: 她的建议对我而言是无价的。
words.en: If you describe something as invaluable, you mean that it is extremely useful.

words.tr: adj. 永无变化的；始终如一的
words.ex: The speed of light is invariable.
words.ex_cn: 光速是不变的。
words.en: An invariable thing or quality never changes or is always the same.

words.ex: The invasion of privacy is a serious problem.
words.ex_cn: 侵犯隐私是一个严重的问题。
words.en: An invasion is an instance of invading a country or region with an armed force.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.ex: The investigator asked the witness a few simple questions.
words.ex_cn: 调查员问了证人几个简单的问题。
words.en: An investigator is someone whose job is to investigate a crime, accident, or other matter.

words.tr: adj. 不容亵渎的；不可侵犯的
words.ex: Her privacy is inviolable.
words.ex_cn: 她的隐私是不可侵犯的。
words.en: If a law or principle is inviolable, it must not be broken or treated without respect.

words.ex: The ghost is invisible to the human eye.
words.ex_cn: 这个鬼魂肉眼看不见。
words.en: If something is invisible, you cannot see it because it is hidden or because it is very difficult to see.

words.tr: v. 邀请；“invite”的现在分词； adj. 诱人的；吸引人的；
words.ex: He is inviting his friends to dinner.
words.ex_cn: 他正在邀请他的朋友来吃晚饭。
words.en: If you describe something as inviting, you mean that it has good qualities that attract you or make you want to experience it.

words.ex: The ship sailed inward toward the harbor.
words.ex_cn: 船向港口内航行。
words.en: Directed or moving towards the inside; relating to the inside or inner part of something.

words.ex: She loves Irish music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢爱尔兰音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Irish means belonging or relating to Ireland, or to its people, language, or culture.

words.ex: It's an irony that the fire station burned down.
words.ex_cn: 消防站着火了，这真是讽刺。
words.en: Irony is a subtle form of humor which involves saying things that you do not mean.

words.ex: The shape has irregular sides.
words.ex_cn: 这个形状的边是不规则的。
words.en: Something that is irregular does not follow the expected pattern, plan, or method; it is not regular.

words.tr: adj. 无关紧要的；不相关的；
words.ex: His opinion is irrelevant to the decision.
words.ex_cn: 他的意见与这个决定无关紧要。
words.en: If you describe something as irrelevant, you mean that it is not important to or not connected with the present situation or discussion.

words.ex: Farmers irrigate their fields with water from the river.
words.ex_cn: 农民用河里的水灌溉他们的田地。
words.en: To supply land or crops with water by means of channels or pipes.

words.ex: He is irritable when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候容易烦躁。
words.en: If someone is irritable, they are easily annoyed.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.tr: adj. 惹人生气的； v. “irritate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The loud noise is irritating.
words.ex_cn: 这噪音很惹人生气。
words.en: If you describe something as irritating, you mean that it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: The irritation on his arm hurt when he touched it.
words.ex_cn: 他手臂上的疼痛处一碰就疼。
words.en: Irritation is the feeling of annoyance, especially when something keeps happening that you do not like.

words.ex: He practices islam every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天 practicing 伊斯兰教。
words.en: Islam is the religion of the Muslims, a monotheistic faith regarded as revealed through Muhammad as the Prophet of Allah.

words.ex: The small isle is surrounded by blue sea.
words.ex_cn: 这个小岛被蓝色的海洋环绕着。
words.en: An isle is a small island.

words.tr:
n. 问题；重要议题；发行（物）；
v. 发行；
words.ex: The main issue is lack of money.
words.ex_cn: 主要问题是缺乏资金。
words.en: An issue is an important subject or problem that people are talking about or arguing about.

words.ex: The word 'hello' is written in italic.
words.ex_cn: 单词 'hello' 是用斜体写的。
words.en: Italic refers to a style of printing or writing in which the letters slope to the right.

words.ex: The book title is in italics.
words.ex_cn: 书名是用斜体写的。
words.en: Italics are a style of font where the letters slant to the right. They are often used to emphasize words, to indicate titles of works, or to denote foreign words.

words.tr: n. 象牙；象牙色 adj. 象牙色的
words.ex: The old piano has ivory keys.
words.ex_cn: 这架旧钢琴有象牙键。
words.en: Ivory is a hard, white material from the tusks and teeth of animals, which is used to make or decorate objects.

words.ex: She wore a necklace made of jade.
words.ex_cn: 她戴着一条玉制的项链。
words.en: A hard, typically green stone used for ornaments and implements and consisting of the minerals jadeite or nephrite.

words.ex: The janitor cleans the school every night.
words.ex_cn: 门卫每天晚上打扫学校。
words.en: A janitor is a person whose job is to take care of a building, especially by cleaning it.

words.ex: She stored jam in a glass jar.
words.ex_cn: 她把果酱存放在一个玻璃罐里。
words.en: A jar is a glass or clay container with a wide opening at the top and a lid, used especially for storing food.

words.ex: He hurt his jaw when he fell.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒时伤到了下巴。
words.en: The jaw is the part of your face below your mouth that moves when you eat or speak.

words.ex: He ate jelly with bread for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃面包配果冻。
words.en: A sweet, clear, semisolid, somewhat elastic spread or dessert made from fruit syrup and pectin or gelatin.

words.ex: He gave the rope a sudden jerk to pull it up.
words.ex_cn: 他猛地一拉绳子，把它拉了上来。
words.en: If you jerk something or someone in a particular direction, or they jerk in a particular direction, they move a short distance very suddenly and quickly.

words.ex: Jesus is central to Christian beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 耶稣是基督教信仰的核心。
words.en: Jesus is the central figure of Christianity, believed by Christians to be the Son of God and the savior of humanity.

words.ex: The jet flew high above the clouds.
words.ex_cn: 喷气式飞机在云层上方飞行。
words.en: A jet is an aircraft that is powered by jet engines, allowing it to fly at high speeds. It can also refer to a stream of liquid or gas forced out of a small opening, or to travel by jet aircraft.

words.ex: He is a jew who celebrates Passover.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位庆祝逾越节的犹太人。
words.en: A Jew is a person whose religion is Judaism, or who is descended from the ancient Hebrew people.

words.tr: adj. 高兴的；快乐的；令人愉快的
words.ex: The children are joyful at the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在派对上很快乐。
words.en: Feeling, expressing, or causing great pleasure and happiness.

words.tr: adj. 充满快乐的；使人高兴的
words.ex: The children were joyous on Christmas morning.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在圣诞节早上非常快乐。
words.en: If you describe something as joyous, you mean that it is full of joy and happiness.

words.tr: adj. 司法的；法庭的；审判的；
words.ex: The judicial system protects people's rights.
words.ex_cn: 司法系统保护人民的权利。
words.en: Judicial means relating to the legal system and to judgments made in a court of law.

words.ex: He poured milk from a jug.
words.ex_cn: 他从一个水壶里倒牛奶。
words.en: A jug is a container used for holding and pouring liquids. It typically has a handle and a spout for easy pouring.

words.tr: adj. 多汁的；利润丰厚的；有趣味的
words.ex: The apple is juicy and sweet.
words.ex_cn: 这个苹果多汁又甜。
words.en: If you describe something as juicy, you mean that it is very interesting or exciting, especially because it involves scandalous or personal information.

words.tr:
adj. （职位或等级）较低的；年幼的；（高中、大学的）三年级学生；
n. 年幼者；
words.ex: He is a junior employee in the company.
words.ex_cn: 他是公司里职位较低的员工。
words.en: A junior person is younger or has a lower position than another person.

words.tr: n. 废旧杂物；无价值的东西；
words.ex: He cleaned up the junk in his garage.
words.ex_cn: 他清理了车库里那些废旧杂物。
words.en: Old or discarded articles that are considered useless or of little value.

words.ex: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
words.ex_cn: 木星是我们太阳系中最大的行星。
words.en: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system, known for its prominent Great Red Spot and numerous moons.

words.ex: The jury decided the man was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团裁定这个人无罪。
words.en: A jury is a group of people who are chosen to decide whether someone is guilty or not guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.ex: He tried to justify his mistake by saying he was tired.
words.ex_cn: 他试图以自己累了为由来证明自己的错误是正当的。
words.en: To justify something means to show or prove that it is reasonable, necessary, or correct.

words.ex: The child looked through the kaleidoscope and laughed.
words.ex_cn: 孩子透过万花筒看，笑了。
words.en: A kaleidoscope is a toy consisting of a tube containing mirrors and pieces of colored glass or paper, whose reflections produce changing patterns when the tube is rotated. It can also refer to a constantly changing pattern or sequence of elements.

words.ex: We sang songs using karaoke at the party.
words.ex_cn: 我们在聚会上用卡拉OK录音唱歌。
words.en: A form of entertainment in which people sing popular songs without the original vocals, typically following the lyrics on a video screen.

words.tr: n. 克拉（宝石重量单位）；开（含纯金的量）
words.ex: The diamond weighs two carats.
words.ex_cn: 这颗钻石重两克拉。
words.en: A unit of weight for precious stones and pearls, equivalent to 200 milligrams.

words.ex: He practices karate every evening.
words.ex_cn: 他每天晚上练习空手道。
words.en: A Japanese martial art in which sharp blows and kicks are administered to pressure-sensitive points on the body of an opponent.

words.tr: adj. 渴望的；热心的；敏锐的；
words.ex: He is keen to learn English.
words.ex_cn: 他渴望学习英语。
words.en: If you are keen on doing something, you very much want to do it. If you are keen that something should happen, you very much want it to happen.

words.ex: The zoo keeper feeds the lions every morning.
words.ex_cn: 动物园饲养员每天早上喂狮子。
words.en: A keeper is someone whose job is to look after a particular place or thing.

words.ex: He uses kerosene to light the lamp.
words.ex_cn: 他用煤油来点灯。
words.en: Kerosene is a type of fuel oil that is used in lamps, heaters, and jet engines.

words.ex: He put ketchup on his fries.
words.ex_cn: 他在薯条上放了番茄酱。
words.en: A thick, smooth sauce made from tomatoes, vinegar, sugar, and spices, used as a condiment.

words.ex: She put the kettle on to make tea.
words.ex_cn: 她把水壶放在炉子上烧水泡茶。
words.en: A kettle is a container or device in which water is boiled, having a lid, spout, and handle, used for making tea or coffee.

words.ex: He looked through the keyhole to see who was outside.
words.ex_cn: 他通过锁孔往外看，想知道谁在外面。
words.en: A keyhole is the hole in a lock that you put a key in to lock or unlock it.

words.tr:
n. 主音；基调；主题
v. 给…定下基调；说明基本政策；作主旨发言
words.ex: The piano played the keynote of the song.
words.ex_cn: 钢琴演奏了这首歌曲的主音。
words.en: The main theme or idea in a speech, book, or discussion.

words.tr:
adj. 土黄色的；卡其布的
n. 卡其布；土黄色
words.ex: He wears khaki pants to work.
words.ex_cn: 他上班穿卡其色裤子。
words.en: A strong, yellowish-brown cloth, used especially for military uniforms.

words.tr:
v. 绑架；劫持；诱拐
n. 绑架罪
words.ex: The man tried to kidnap the little girl.
words.ex_cn: 这个人试图绑架那个小女孩。
words.en: To take someone away illegally by force, typically to obtain a ransom.

words.ex: The kidnapper took the boy and demanded money.
words.ex_cn: 绑匪绑架了那个男孩并索要赎金。
words.en: A kidnapper is a person who abducts someone and holds them captive, typically to demand a ransom.

words.ex: He drank water to help his kidney work better.
words.ex_cn: 他喝水以帮助肾脏更好地工作。
words.en: One of the two organs in your lower back that separate waste products from your blood and make urine.

words.ex: The file is 5 kilobytes big.
words.ex_cn: 这个文件有5千字节大小。
words.en: A kilobyte is a unit of digital information storage or transmission with the value of 1,024 bytes.

words.ex: She is kind-hearted and helps her neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 她心地善良，总是帮助邻居。
words.en: If you describe someone as kind-hearted, you mean that they are kind, caring, and generous.

words.tr: v. 点燃；生火；激起；发亮
words.ex: He used a match to kindle the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: To kindle something means to cause it to begin burning or to arouse or inspire it.

words.tr: n. 售货亭；报刊亭；公用电话亭
words.ex: He bought a ticket from the kiosk.
words.ex_cn: 他从自动售票机买了一张票。
words.en: A kiosk is a small open-fronted hut or cubicle from which newspapers, refreshments, tickets, etc., are sold.

words.ex: The kitten is sleeping on the sofa.
words.ex_cn: 小猫正在沙发上睡觉。
words.en: A kitten is a very young cat.

words.ex: He put his books in a knapsack and walked to school.
words.ex_cn: 他把书放进背包，然后走路去学校。
words.en: A knapsack is a bag carried on the back, typically made of a strong, waterproof material and used by hikers and soldiers.

words.tr: n. 骑士（爵士）资格（地位、身份）；骑士精神
words.ex: He received knighthood for his service to medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他因对医学的贡献而被授予骑士头衔。
words.en: The rank or title of a knight; the qualities befitting a knight, such as bravery, courtesy, honor, and gallantry toward women.

words.ex: She knit a warm scarf for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为她的弟弟织了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

words.ex: He turned the knob to adjust the volume.
words.ex_cn: 他转动旋钮来调节音量。
words.en: A knob is a round handle, or a round switch on a piece of equipment.

words.ex: He tied a knot in the rope.
words.ex_cn: 他在绳子上打了一个结。
words.en: A knot is a fastening made by tying a piece of string, rope, or something similar. It can also refer to a hard mass formed in a tree trunk at the intersection with a branch, or a unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour, used especially by ships and aircraft.

words.ex: He is knowledgeable about history and science.
words.ex_cn: 他对历史和科学都很博学。
words.en: Someone who is knowledgeable has or shows a clear understanding of many different facts about the world or about a particular subject.

words.tr:
n. 指关节
v. 用指关节…；屈从
words.ex: He cracked his knuckles before the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛前掰响了指关节。
words.en: The knuckles are the joints of the fingers, especially where they join the hand.

words.tr: v. 磕头；叩头；卑躬屈膝；唯命是从
words.ex: He refused to kowtow to the boss's unfair demands.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝向老板的不公平要求卑躬屈膝。
words.en: To kowtow means to show too much respect to someone in authority, often by doing whatever they tell you to do.

words.ex: He practices kung fu every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上练习功夫。
words.en: Kung fu refers to the Chinese martial arts, which are a series of fighting styles that have developed over the centuries in China.

words.tr: n. 迷宫；难解的事件；错综复杂；
words.ex: The child got lost in the labyrinth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在迷宫里迷路了。
words.en: A labyrinth is a complicated irregular network of passages or paths in which it is difficult to find one's way; a maze.

words.tr:
n. 地方；方位；
v. 安放；安置；
words.ex: This is a quiet place to read books.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个安静的地方读书。
words.en: A particular position or point in space.

words.ex: The lad is playing soccer with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 那个男孩正在和朋友们踢足球。
words.en: A lad is a young man or boy.

words.ex: A ladybird is sitting on the leaf.
words.ex_cn: 一只瓢虫正停在叶子上。
words.en: A ladybird is a small beetle with a round body, typically red or yellow with black spots.

words.tr:
n. 滞后；延迟；
v. 落后；缓慢移动；
words.ex: There is a lag between the signal and the response.
words.ex_cn: 信号和响应之间有滞后。
words.en: If one thing or person lags behind another thing or person, their progress is slower than that of the other.

words.tr:
adj. 瘸的；跛的；站不住脚的；无说服力的
v. 变跛；瘸行
words.ex: The lame dog walked slowly on three legs.
words.ex_cn: 那只瘸狗用三条腿慢慢走。
words.en: If someone is lame, they are unable to walk properly because of damage to one or both of their legs. A lame excuse, explanation, etc. is one that is weak and difficult to believe.

words.tr: n. 着陆；降落；楼梯平台； v. “land”的现在分词；
words.ex: The plane made a smooth landing at the airport.
words.ex_cn: 飞机在机场平稳着陆。
words.en: The act of coming to or bringing something to land, especially an aircraft.

words.ex: The invention of the wheel was a landmark in human history.
words.ex_cn: 轮子的发明是人类历史上的一个里程碑。
words.en: A landmark is a building or feature of a landscape that is easily seen and recognized from a distance, especially one that enables someone to establish their location.

words.ex: The landscape after the rain is very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 雨后的景色非常美丽。
words.en: A landscape is all the visible features of an area of land, often considered in terms of their aesthetic appeal.

words.tr: n. 小路；小巷；航道；车道；航线；
words.ex: The children walked down the narrow lane to school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们沿着狭窄的小路去上学。
words.en: A lane is a narrow road, especially in the country. It can also refer to a division of a road intended to separate lines of traffic moving in the same or opposite directions.

words.ex: The children carried paper lanterns at the festival.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在节日上提着纸灯笼。
words.en: A lantern is a lamp in a container that has a handle for holding or hanging it, and it usually has a protective case around the flame or bulb.

words.tr: n. 一圈；（人坐着时）大腿部；
words.ex: He ran three laps around the track.
words.ex_cn: 他在跑道上跑了三圈。
words.en: The upper part of the legs of a seated person; a single turn or round in a race or other competition.

words.tr: n. 云雀；百灵鸟；玩乐；嬉戏
words.ex: The lark sings loudly at sunrise.
words.ex_cn: 云雀在日出时大声歌唱。
words.en: A lark is a small brown bird that is known for its beautiful song. It is also used to describe a carefree adventure or a playful activity.

words.ex: The butterfly starts as a larva.
words.ex_cn: 蝴蝶从幼虫开始。
words.en: An insect in the stage of development when it has just come out of an egg and before it changes into its adult form.

words.ex: The doctor used a laser to fix her eye.
words.ex_cn: 医生用激光修复了她的眼睛。
words.en: A laser is a device that emits light through a process of optical amplification based on the stimulated emission of electromagnetic radiation.

words.tr: n. 课；班级；等级；阶级；类别；
words.ex: I have math class at 9 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 我上午九点有数学课。
words.en: A class is a group of pupils or students who are taught together.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.ex: The city is at a latitude of 40 degrees north.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市位于北纬40度。
words.en: Latitude is the distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees.

words.tr:
v. 发射；发起；启动；
n. 发射；投掷；启动；
words.ex: They will launch a rocket tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天将发射一枚火箭。
words.en: To launch something means to send it into the air, space, or water, especially with a lot of force or effort, or to start an activity, event, or project.

words.tr: n. 要洗的衣物；洗衣店；
words.ex: I put the dirty laundry in the washing machine.
words.ex_cn: 我把脏衣服放进洗衣机里。
words.en: Laundry refers to the clothes and linens that need to be washed or that have just been washed. It can also refer to the place or business where clothes and linens are washed and ironed.

words.ex: He is a Nobel laureate for his poetry.
words.ex_cn: 他因诗歌而获得诺贝尔奖。
words.en: A laureate is someone who has been given a prize or honor for achievement in a particular field, especially in the arts or sciences.

words.ex: The volcano spilled hot lava down the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 火山喷出炽热的岩浆流下山。
words.en: Lava is the molten rock that comes out of a volcano during an eruption.

words.ex: The lavatory is down the hall.
words.ex_cn: 洗手间在走廊尽头。
words.en: A lavatory is a room equipped with a toilet and sink for washing hands and face.

words.ex: The children play on the lawn after school.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们放学后在草坪上玩耍。
words.en: A lawn is an area of grass that is kept cut short and is usually part of someone's garden or yard, or part of a park.

words.ex: The cake has three layers of chocolate.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕有三层巧克力。
words.en: A layer of a substance or material is a quantity or piece of it that covers a surface or that is between two other things.

words.ex: The doctor explained the disease in layman terms.
words.ex_cn: 医生用通俗易懂的语言解释了这种疾病。
words.en: A layman is a person who does not have specialized or professional knowledge of a subject.

words.ex: The layout of the room makes it feel bigger.
words.ex_cn: 房间的布局让它显得更大。
words.en: The way in which the parts of something are arranged or laid out.

words.ex: He handed out a leaflet about the event.
words.ex_cn: 他分发了一份关于该活动的传单。
words.en: A leaflet is a small sheet of printed paper that gives you information or advertises something.

words.tr:
n. 漏洞；泄露；
v. 漏；泄露；
words.ex: The leak in the roof caused water to drip inside.
words.ex_cn: 屋顶的漏洞导致水滴进屋里。
words.en: If a container or pipe leaks, or if it leaks a substance such as liquid or gas, the substance comes out of it accidentally because there is a hole or crack in it.

words.tr:
n. 跳跃；
v. 跳跃；
words.ex: The cat made a big leap over the fence.
words.ex_cn: 猫跳过了篱笆。
words.en: To leap means to jump high or a long way, or to move quickly and with a lot of energy.

words.tr:
n. 租契；
v. 出租；
words.ex: He signed a lease for the apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他签了公寓的租契。
words.en: A lease is a legal agreement by which the owner of a building, a piece of land, or something such as a car allows someone else to use it for a period of time in return for money.

words.ex: He writes all the money in the ledger.
words.ex_cn: 他把所有的钱都记在账本上。
words.en: A ledger is a book or collection of accounts in which account transactions are recorded.

words.ex: The sailors found shelter on the lee side of the island.
words.ex_cn: 水手们在岛屿的背风处找到了庇护。
words.en: The side or part that is sheltered or protected from the wind.

words.tr:
adj. 剩余的；
n. 残留物；
words.ex: We ate the leftover food for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 我们早餐吃了剩下的食物。
words.en: Remaining after the rest has been used, consumed, or dealt with.

words.ex: His legacy includes many charity schools.
words.ex_cn: 他的遗产包括许多慈善学校。
words.en: Something handed down from an ancestor or a predecessor or from the past.

words.ex: The legend says a dragon lives in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 传说有一条龙住在山里。
words.en: A legend is a very old and popular story that may be true or may be imaginary.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.tr: adj. 立法的；制定法律的；
words.ex: The legislative branch makes laws.
words.ex_cn: 立法部门制定法律。
words.en: Relating to the making of laws.

words.ex: The legislature passed a new law last week.
words.ex_cn: 立法机构上周通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A legislature is the part of a country's government that is responsible for making laws.

words.ex: He reads books in his leisure.
words.ex_cn: 他在空闲时间读书。
words.en: Leisure is the time when you are not working and you can relax and do things that you enjoy.

words.tr: n. 柠檬汽水；柠檬饮料
words.ex: He drinks lemonade every afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他每天下午喝柠檬水。
words.en: A drink made from lemon juice, water, and sugar.

words.ex: The camera has a clear lens.
words.ex_cn: 这台相机有一个清晰的透镜。
words.en: A lens is a piece of curved glass or other transparent substance that is used in things such as cameras, telescopes, or pairs of glasses to make images larger or smaller.

words.ex: The leopard runs fast in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 豹在野外跑得很快。
words.en: A large wild cat that has a yellowish-brown or brown coat with black spots, found in Africa and southern Asia.

words.ex: Try to lessen your sugar intake.
words.ex_cn: 试着减少你的糖摄入量。
words.en: If something lessens or you lessen it, it becomes smaller in size, amount, degree, or importance.

words.ex: He spoke quietly lest he wake the baby.
words.ex_cn: 他低声说话，以免吵醒婴儿。
words.en: If you do something lest something unpleasant should happen, you do it to try to prevent the unpleasant thing from happening.

words.ex: She added lettuce to her sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 她在三明治里加了莴苣。
words.en: Lettuce is a plant with large green leaves that is eaten in salads.

words.ex: The levee held back the floodwaters, preventing a disaster.
words.ex_cn: 堤坝挡住了洪水，防止了一场灾难。
words.en: A levee is an embankment built to prevent the overflow of a river.

words.ex: The clever boy solved the math problem quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这个聪明的男孩很快解决了这道数学题。
words.en: Someone who is clever is intelligent and able to understand things easily or plan things well.

words.ex: He is a reliable friend who always helps.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个可靠的朋友，总是帮忙。
words.en: Able to be trusted to do or provide what is needed or right.

words.ex: He is the liaison between the two departments.
words.ex_cn: 他是两个部门之间的联络人。
words.en: A liaison is a person who acts as a link to assist communication between different groups or organizations.

words.ex: He believes in liberalism and supports personal freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他相信自由主义，支持个人自由。
words.en: Liberalism is a political and moral philosophy based on liberty, consent of the governed, and equality before the law.

words.ex: They will liberate the prisoners tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他们明天会释放这些囚犯。
words.en: To liberate a place or the people in it means to free them from the political or military control of another country, area, or group of people.

words.ex: The liberation of the city ended the war.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市的解放结束了战争。
words.en: Liberation refers to the act of setting someone free from imprisonment, slavery, or oppression; release.

words.ex: The address is 720 liberty street.
words.ex_cn: 地址是自由大街720号。
words.en: The state of being free within society from oppressive restrictions imposed by authority on one's way of life, behavior, or political views.

words.ex: Lichen grows on old rocks.
words.ex_cn: 地衣生长在古老的岩石上。
words.en: Lichen is a simple slow-growing plant that typically forms a low crusty, leaflike, or branching growth on rocks, walls, and trees.

words.tr: n. 代理；副手；（陆军）中尉；（海军）上尉
words.ex: He acted as lieutenant for the manager while she was away.
words.ex_cn: 当经理离开时，他担任代理。
words.en: A lieutenant is a person who holds a junior officer's rank in the armed forces, or a person who acts as a deputy to a superior.

words.ex: I like coffee, and she likes it likewise.
words.ex_cn: 我喜欢咖啡，她也喜欢。
words.en: You use likewise when you are comparing two methods, states, or situations and saying that they are similar.

words.tr: n. 嗜好；爱好； v. “like”的现在分词；
words.ex: His liking for chocolate is very strong.
words.ex_cn: 他对巧克力的嗜好非常强烈。
words.en: If you have a liking for something, you enjoy it or approve of it.

words.ex: She planted a white lily in her garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里种了一朵白色的百合。
words.en: A lily is a plant with large flowers that are often white, but can also be pink, yellow, or purple. Lilies are commonly used in gardens and as cut flowers.

words.ex: The child hurt his limb while playing.
words.ex_cn: 孩子玩耍时伤到了肢体。
words.en: A limb is one of the jointed appendages of an animal used for locomotion or grasping: arm; leg; wing; flipper.

words.ex: Farmers spread lime on the soil to make it less acidic.
words.ex_cn: 农民在土壤上撒石灰以降低其酸性。
words.en: Lime is a white substance obtained by heating limestone, used in making cement and in farming to improve soil. It is also a small green fruit that is similar to a lemon.

words.ex: The building is made of limestone.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑是由石灰岩建造的。
words.en: Limestone is a sedimentary rock composed largely of the mineral calcite (calcium carbonate: CaCO3).

words.ex: He rode in a limousine to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他坐豪华轿车去参加婚礼。
words.en: A limousine is a large, luxurious car, especially one driven by a chauffeur and having a partition separating the passengers from the driver.

words.tr:
v. 跛行；蹒跚；瘸着走
adj. 无力的；无生气的
words.ex: He limps after hurting his leg.
words.ex_cn: 他受伤后走路一瘸一拐。
words.en: If someone limps, they walk with difficulty or in an uneven way because one of their legs or feet is hurt.

words.ex: The graph shows a linear relationship between time and distance.
words.ex_cn: 这张图显示了时间与距离之间的线性关系。
words.en: Linear means involving or relating to a straight line or lines.

words.ex: She washed the linen in cold water.
words.ex_cn: 她用冷水洗亚麻布。
words.en: Linen is a kind of cloth that is made from the fibers of the flax plant. It is used to make clothes, sheets, and tablecloths.

words.ex: The liner sailed across the ocean with hundreds of passengers.
words.ex_cn: 这艘邮轮载着数百名乘客横渡了海洋。
words.en: A liner is a large ship that carries passengers on regular journeys.

words.tr: n. 通晓数国语言的人；语言学家；
words.ex: He is a linguist who speaks five languages.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位通晓五种语言的人。
words.en: A linguist is someone who studies language or languages, especially a person who studies linguistics.

words.ex: He is interested in linguistic patterns in children.
words.ex_cn: 他对儿童的语言模式感兴趣。
words.en: Relating to language or linguistics.

words.ex: He is studying linguistics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习语言学。
words.en: Linguistics is the scientific study of language and its structure, including the study of morphology, syntax, phonetics, and semantics.

words.ex: The lioness hunts for her cubs every day.
words.ex_cn: 母狮每天为她的幼崽捕猎。
words.en: A lioness is a female lion.

words.ex: She put on red lipstick before the party.
words.ex_cn: 她在派对前涂了红色口红。
words.en: Lipstick is a colored substance in the form of a stick, used for coloring the lips.

words.tr:
n. 液体；
adj. 液态的；
words.ex: Water is a common liquid.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种常见的液体。
words.en: A liquid is a substance which is not solid but which flows and can be poured, for example water.

words.ex: He eats too much sugar and his liver is hurt.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多糖，他的肝脏受损了。
words.en: The liver is a large organ in the body that cleans the blood and produces bile, or a person who lives in a particular way.

words.ex: We waited in the hotel lobby for our friend.
words.ex_cn: 我们在酒店的大厅里等我们的朋友。
words.en: A lobby is a large room or hall in a building, often used for meetings or as a waiting area. As a verb, to lobby means to try to influence politicians or officials on a particular issue.

words.ex: He bought a fresh lobster at the market.
words.ex_cn: 他在市场上买了一只新鲜的龙虾。
words.en: A lobster is a sea creature with a hard shell, two large claws, and eight legs, or the flesh of this animal eaten as food.

words.ex: The locality has many small shops and cafes.
words.ex_cn: 这个地区有许多小商店和咖啡馆。
words.en: A locality is a particular place or area, especially in relation to its geographical position or features.

words.ex: The locomotive pulled the train down the track.
words.ex_cn: 机车拉着火车沿着轨道行驶。
words.en: A locomotive is a powered rail vehicle used for pulling trains.

words.ex: The locust flew over the field.
words.ex_cn: 蝗虫飞过了田野。
words.en: A locust is a large insect that lives in hot countries and flies in large groups, destroying crops.

words.ex: They stayed in a small lodge near the forest.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在森林附近的一座小屋里。
words.en: A lodge is a small house in the country, especially one that is used by people on holiday or by people taking part in a sport such as skiing or hunting. As a verb, to lodge means to stay somewhere, especially temporarily, or to formally submit something, such as a complaint or an application.

words.tr: n. 寄宿处； v. “lodge”的现在分词；
words.ex: He found cheap lodging near the train station.
words.ex_cn: 他在火车站附近找到了便宜的寄宿处。
words.en: Lodging refers to a place to live or stay, especially temporarily.

words.tr: adj. 高的；崇高的；傲慢的
words.ex: The mountain has a lofty peak.
words.ex_cn: 这座山有一个很高的山顶。
words.en: If you say that someone behaves in a lofty way, you are critical of them for behaving in a proud and rather unpleasant way, as if they think they are very important.

words.tr:
n. 原木；航海日志；
v. （正式地）记载；
words.ex: The fire burned brightly with a large log.
words.ex_cn: 大火用一根大原木烧得很旺。
words.en: A log is a piece of a thick branch or trunk of a tree that has been cut so that it can be used for fuel or for making things. A log is also a written record of events, often on a ship or aircraft.

words.ex: He uses logic to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他用逻辑来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Logic is a method of reasoning that involves a series of statements, each of which must be true if the statement before it is true.

words.ex: He felt lonesome after his dog died.
words.ex_cn: 他的狗去世后，他感到孤独。
words.en: If you are lonesome, you are unhappy because you are alone or because you have no friends or family with you.

words.ex: Eating healthy food helps with longevity.
words.ex_cn: 健康饮食有助于长寿。
words.en: Longevity refers to the length or duration of an individual's life, especially when it is unusually long.

words.ex: The ship's longitude is 45 degrees west.
words.ex_cn: 这艘船的经度是西经45度。
words.en: Longitude is the distance of a place east or west of the Greenwich meridian, measured in degrees.

words.tr:
n. 织布机；
v. 迫近；
words.ex: The old loom made a loud clicking sound.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧织布机发出很大的咔嗒声。
words.en: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a way that is frightening or causes worry.

words.ex: He drew a loop with the pencil.
words.ex_cn: 他用铅笔画了一个圈。
words.en: A loop is a shape produced by a curve that bends round and crosses itself, or a piece of wire, string, etc. that has this shape. It can also refer to a repeated sequence of operations or events in a computer program or in a process.

words.ex: He tried to loosen the tight screw.
words.ex_cn: 他试图拧松那颗紧的螺丝。
words.en: If you loosen something or if it loosens, it becomes less tight, less firmly fixed, or less strongly attached.

words.ex: He bought a lottery ticket last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周买了一张彩票。
words.en: A lottery is a type of gambling game in which people buy numbered tickets. Several numbers are then chosen, and the people who have those numbers on their tickets win a prize.

words.ex: We waited in the lounge before our flight.
words.ex_cn: 我们在登机前等在休息室里。
words.en: A lounge is a room in a house or public building where people can sit and relax. As a verb, to lounge means to lie, sit, or stand in a relaxed or lazy way.

words.ex: She is a lovable and kind-hearted person.
words.ex_cn: 她是一个可爱且心地善良的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as lovable, you mean that they have attractive qualities, and are easy to like.

words.ex: His loyalty to his friends never changed.
words.ex_cn: 他对朋友的忠诚从未改变。
words.en: The quality of being loyal to someone or something.

words.ex: Oil helps to lubricate the engine parts.
words.ex_cn: 油有助于润滑发动机部件。
words.en: To apply a substance such as oil or grease to (something) in order to minimize friction and allow smooth movement.

words.ex: The factory buys lumber to make furniture.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂购买木材来制造家具。
words.en: Lumber refers to wood that has been processed into beams and planks, a stage in the process of wood production. It is also used to describe the action of moving in a slow, heavy, awkward way.

words.ex: The lunar surface is covered with dust.
words.ex_cn: 月球表面覆盖着尘土。
words.en: Of or relating to the moon.

words.ex: The lunatic was taken to the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 那个疯人被送到了医院。
words.en: A lunatic is someone who behaves in a crazy or very foolish way.

words.ex: We had a quick luncheon at the café.
words.ex_cn: 我们在咖啡馆简单吃了顿午餐。
words.en: A luncheon is a formal lunch, or a formal word for lunch.

words.tr:
n. 鲁特琴；古琵琶；诗琴；封泥
v. 用封泥盖、包或密封
words.ex: He plays the lute in the evening.
words.ex_cn: 他晚上弹鲁特琴。
words.en: A lute is a stringed musical instrument with a body shaped like a pear and a neck with a fretted fingerboard, played by plucking the strings.

words.tr: n. 胶布雨衣；马金托什雨衣
words.ex: He wears a mackintosh when it rains.
words.ex_cn: 天下雨时，他穿一件雨衣。
words.en: A mackintosh is a coat made from material that does not let rain in, or the material itself.

words.ex: The magician pulled a rabbit from a hat.
words.ex_cn: 魔术师从帽子里变出了一只兔子。
words.en: A magician is a person who performs magic tricks to entertain people, often as part of a show.

words.ex: Magnesium helps muscles work properly.
words.ex_cn: 镁有助于肌肉正常运作。
words.en: Magnesium is a silver-white metallic element that is essential for human nutrition and is used in various industrial applications.

words.ex: The magnet picks up the iron nail.
words.ex_cn: 磁铁吸起了铁钉。
words.en: A magnet is a piece of iron or other material which attracts iron or steel towards it.

words.ex: The magnet has a magnetic force.
words.ex_cn: 这块磁铁有磁性。
words.en: If you describe something as magnetic, you mean that it is very attractive to people because it has unusual, powerful, and exciting qualities.

words.ex: The sunset over the mountains was magnificent.
words.ex_cn: 山上的日落壮丽极了。
words.en: If you say that something or someone is magnificent, you mean that you think they are extremely good, beautiful, or impressive.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: The table is made of mahogany.
words.ex_cn: 这张桌子是用桃花心木制成的。
words.en: Mahogany is a type of hardwood that is reddish-brown in color and is used for making furniture.

words.ex: It was her maiden flight on a plane.
words.ex_cn: 这是她第一次坐飞机。
words.en: A maiden is a young girl or woman who is not married.

words.ex: He put the letter in the mailbox.
words.ex_cn: 他把信放进邮箱里。
words.en: A mailbox is a box outside your house where your letters are delivered. It can also refer to a similar box where you can post letters.

words.ex: He moved from the island to the mainland for work.
words.ex_cn: 他从岛屿搬到大陆工作。
words.en: The mainland is the main part of a country or continent, as opposed to islands or peninsulas.

words.ex: Pop music is part of the mainstream.
words.ex_cn: 流行音乐是主流的一部分。
words.en: The ideas, attitudes, or activities that are shared by most people and regarded as normal or conventional.

words.ex: The cost of maintenance is low for this car.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的维持费用很低。
words.en: The process of preserving a condition or situation or the state of being preserved.

words.ex: He grows maize on his farm.
words.ex_cn: 他在农场种植玉米。
words.en: Maize is a tall plant which produces long objects covered with yellow seeds called sweetcorn. It is often grown as a food crop.

words.tr: n. 最高权威；王权；威严
words.ex: The king showed his majesty to the crowd.
words.ex_cn: 国王向人群展示了他的威严。
words.en: If you talk about the majesty of something, you are emphasizing its great beauty, scale, or power.

words.ex: He has a rare malady that doctors are trying to cure.
words.ex_cn: 他患有一种罕见的疾病，医生们正在努力治疗。
words.en: A malady is a disease or illness.

words.ex: He got malaria from a mosquito bite.
words.ex_cn: 他被蚊子叮咬后得了疟疾。
words.en: Malaria is a disease caused by a parasite that is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected mosquitoes.

words.ex: He acted out of malice, not mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于恶意，而不是错误。
words.en: Malice is behavior that is intended to harm people or their reputations, or cause them embarrassment and upset.

words.ex: He sent a malicious email to hurt his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他发了一封怀恶意的邮件来伤害他的朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone's words or actions as malicious, you mean that they are intended to harm people or their reputation, or to cause them embarrassment and upset.

words.ex: He goes to the mall to buy clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他去商场买衣服。
words.en: A mall is a large enclosed shopping area from which traffic is excluded.

words.ex: The child has malnutrition from not eating enough food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子因为吃不够饭而营养不良。
words.en: Malnutrition is a condition that results from eating a diet in which certain nutrients are lacking, in excess (too high in intake), or in the wrong proportions.

words.ex: He maltreats his dog every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都虐待他的狗。
words.en: To maltreat someone means to treat them cruelly or unkindly.

words.ex: A dog is a mammal.
words.ex_cn: 狗是一种哺乳动物。
words.en: A mammal is a type of animal that feeds its young with milk produced by the mother's body. Mammals are warm-blooded and usually have hair or fur.

words.ex: He reached manhood at the age of eighteen.
words.ex_cn: 他十八岁时成年。
words.en: Manhood refers to the state or period of being a man, especially an adult man, and can also denote the qualities traditionally associated with men, such as strength and courage.

words.ex: The garden has manifold flowers.
words.ex_cn: 这个花园里有繁多的花朵。
words.en: If something is manifold, it has many different parts, features, or forms.

words.tr: adj. 有男子气概的；阳刚的；
words.ex: He showed manly courage during the crisis.
words.ex_cn: 他在危机中表现出了男子气概。
words.en: If you describe a man's behaviour or appearance as manly, you mean that it has qualities which are considered typical of a man, such as strength or courage.

words.ex: He lives in a big mansion near the lake.
words.ex_cn: 他住在湖边的一座大宅子里。
words.en: A mansion is a very large, impressive house, especially one that is the home of a wealthy or important person.

words.tr:
n. 制造；
v. （用机器大量）制造；虚构；捏造；
words.ex: The manufacture of cars needs many workers.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的制造需要很多工人。
words.en: To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.

words.ex: He found an old manuscript in the library.
words.ex_cn: 他在图书馆里发现了一份旧手稿。
words.en: A manuscript is a handwritten or typed document, especially a writer's first version of a book before it is published.

words.ex: The maple leaves turn red in autumn.
words.ex_cn: 枫树的叶子在秋天变红。
words.en: A maple is a tree or shrub with lobed leaves, winged fruits, and colorful autumn foliage, which is often cultivated for its sap, wood, or ornamental value.

words.tr: n. 马拉松赛跑；耐力赛；
words.ex: He ran a marathon last Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他上个星期日跑了一场马拉松赛跑。
words.en: A marathon is a long-distance running event with an official distance of 42.195 kilometers (26 miles 385 yards), usually run as a road race. The event was instituted in commemoration of the fabled run of the Greek soldier Pheidippides, a messenger from the Battle of Marathon to Athens.

words.ex: The statue is made of white marble.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像由白色大理石制成。
words.en: Marble is a type of very hard rock which is used for making statues and for building. It is usually white with dark lines in it.

words.tr: n. 人造黄油；人造奶油
words.ex: He puts margarine on his bread every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上在面包上抹人造黄油。
words.en: Margarine is a yellow substance made from vegetable oil and animal fats that is similar to butter. You spread it on bread or use it for cooking.

words.tr: n. 差额；边缘；净利润；余地；
words.ex: The profit margin is five dollars.
words.ex_cn: 利润差额是五美元。
words.en: The margin is the edge or border of something, or the difference between two amounts, especially the difference between the cost of producing something and the price it is sold for.

words.ex: The marine birds fly over the sea.
words.ex_cn: 这些海鸟在海面上飞翔。
words.en: Marine is used to describe things relating to the sea or to the ships and boats which sail on it.

words.ex: The small town has a maritime history.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有着海洋历史。
words.en: Relating to the sea, especially in relation to seaborne trade or naval matters.

words.tr: v. （使）留痕迹；做标记；评分；“mark”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 明显的；显著的；有记号的；
words.ex: The storm marked the old tree with deep scratches.
words.ex_cn: 风暴在那棵老树上留下了深深的划痕。
words.en: A marked change or difference is very obvious and easily noticed.

words.ex: He works in marketing for a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他在一家科技公司从事营销工作。
words.en: Marketing involves the process of promoting, selling, and distributing a product or service. It includes market research and advertising.

words.ex: He eats bread with marmalade for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他早餐吃涂了果酱的面包。
words.en: Marmalade is a sweet food made from fruit, sugar, and water, especially oranges, which is spread on bread or used in cooking.

words.tr: n. 骨髓；精华；活力；西葫芦
words.ex: The bone marrow makes blood cells.
words.ex_cn: 骨髓制造血细胞。
words.en: The soft fatty substance in the cavities of bones, in which blood cells are produced; the essence or most vital part of something.

words.ex: The rover is exploring mars.
words.ex_cn: 探测器正在探索火星。
words.en: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun in the Solar System and the second-smallest planet in the Solar System, after Mercury. Named after the Roman god of war, it is often referred to as the 'Red Planet' because the iron oxide prevalent on its surface gives it a reddish appearance.

words.ex: The birds live in a quiet marsh.
words.ex_cn: 这些鸟生活在一片宁静的沼泽中。
words.en: A marsh is an area of low-lying land which is flooded in wet seasons or at high tide, and typically remains waterlogged at all times.

words.tr:
n. 元帅；高级军官；典礼官；消防局长
v. 整理；集结
words.ex: The marshal led the army into battle.
words.ex_cn: 元帅率领军队上战场。
words.en: A marshal is a high-ranking officer in the armed forces, especially in the army or air force, or a person who arranges or directs a public event.

words.tr:
n. 殉道者；殉教者；烈士
v. 处死；折磨
words.ex: He became a martyr for freedom.
words.ex_cn: 他为自由而成为烈士。
words.en: A martyr is someone who is killed or made to suffer greatly because of their religious or political beliefs, and is admired and respected by people who share those beliefs.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.ex: The view from the hill is marvellous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色绝妙极了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as marvellous, you are emphasizing that they are extremely good, enjoyable, or impressive.

words.ex: He believes in marxism and supports workers' rights.
words.ex_cn: 他相信马克思主义，并支持工人的权利。
words.en: Marxism is a method of socioeconomic analysis that views class relations and social conflict using a materialist interpretation of historical development and takes a dialectical view of social transformation.

words.tr:
adj. 马克思主义的
n. 马克思主义者
words.ex: He is a Marxist who believes in workers' rights.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位相信工人权利的马克思主义者。
words.en: A Marxist is someone who believes in the political and economic theories of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, especially the idea that capitalism will inevitably be replaced by socialism and then communism.

words.ex: He has a masculine voice and strong build.
words.ex_cn: 他声音低沉，身材强壮。
words.en: Having qualities or appearance traditionally associated with men.

words.tr: n. 男性；男子气概；阳性
words.ex: He shows traditional masculinity by being strong and quiet.
words.ex_cn: 他通过坚强和沉默展现男性气质。
words.en: The quality or condition of being masculine; manliness.

words.ex: He wore a scary mask at the Halloween party.
words.ex_cn: 他在万圣节派对上戴了一个可怕的面具。
words.en: A mask is a piece of cloth or other material that you wear over your face to hide or protect it.

words.ex: The mason built a stone wall with care.
words.ex_cn: 石匠仔细地砌了一堵石墙。
words.en: A mason is a person who builds or works with stone or brick.

words.tr:
v. 屠杀 
n. 大屠杀
words.ex: The soldiers committed a massacre in the village.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在村庄里进行了大屠杀。
words.en: The indiscriminate killing of a large number of people.

words.ex: The sailboat's mast is very tall.
words.ex_cn: 帆船的船桅很高。
words.en: A mast is a tall pole on a ship or boat that supports the sails.

words.tr: adj. 母亲的；母性的；母系的；
words.ex: Her maternal love kept the family strong.
words.ex_cn: 她的母爱让家庭保持坚强。
words.en: Maternal feelings or actions are typical of a kind, loving mother.

words.tr:
n. 最大限度；最大量；
adj. 最大极限的；最多的；
words.ex: The maximum of the crowd is 100 people.
words.ex_cn: 人群的上限是100人。
words.en: The greatest or highest amount possible or attained.

words.ex: The mayor walks to work every morning.
words.ex_cn: 市长每天早上步行上班。
words.en: The mayor of a town or city is the person who has been elected to represent it for a fixed period of time, or, in some places, to run its government.

words.ex: The cows are grazing in the meadow.
words.ex_cn: 牛群正在草地上吃草。
words.en: A meadow is a field with grass and often wild flowers in it.

words.ex: The measurement of temperature is important in science.
words.ex_cn: 温度的衡量在科学中很重要。
words.en: The action of measuring something.

words.ex: The mechanic fixed my car quickly.
words.ex_cn: 机修工很快修好了我的车。
words.en: A mechanic is a person whose job is to repair and maintain machines and engines, especially those of vehicles.

words.tr: n. 运作方式；力学；“mechanic”的复数；
words.ex: The mechanics of this machine are simple to understand.
words.ex_cn: 这台机器的运作方式很简单易懂。
words.en: Mechanics is the branch of physics that deals with the action of forces on bodies and with motion, comprised of kinetics, statics, and kinematics.

words.ex: The body has a mechanism to fight viruses.
words.ex_cn: 人体有一种对抗病毒的机制。
words.en: A mechanism is a part of a machine that does a particular task, or a system that is intended to achieve something or deal with a problem.

words.ex: The factory will mechanize its production line next year.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂明年将使生产线实现机械化。
words.en: To mechanize something means to change it so that it is done by machines or mechanical processes rather than by human labor.

words.ex: The castle is a medieval building.
words.ex_cn: 这座城堡是一座中世纪的建筑。
words.en: Relating to the Middle Ages, the period in European history from about the 5th century to the 15th century.

words.ex: He ate a sweet melon for dessert.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了一块甜瓜当甜点。
words.en: A melon is a large, juicy fruit with a hard rind, belonging to the gourd family, typically eaten fresh.

words.ex: The ice melts in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 冰在阳光下融化。
words.en: If a solid substance melts or if you melt it, it changes to a liquid, usually because it has been heated.

words.ex: He wrote a memoir about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他写了一本关于自己童年的回忆录。
words.en: A memoir is a book or article that you write about someone who you have known, describing what you remember of them and of particular events in which you both took part.

words.ex: The broken bridge is a menace to drivers.
words.ex_cn: 这座破桥对司机来说是个危险物。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is a menace, you mean that they are likely to cause serious harm.

words.ex: His mentality changed after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故发生后，他的心理状态发生了变化。
words.en: Your mentality is your attitudes and your way of thinking.

words.ex: The store sells cheap merchandise.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售廉价商品。
words.en: Goods to be bought and sold.

words.ex: The merchant sells fresh fruit every morning.
words.ex_cn: 商人每天早上卖新鲜水果。
words.en: A merchant is a person who buys and sells goods, especially one who owns a shop.

words.tr: adj. 仁慈的；慈悲的；宽大的
words.ex: The judge was merciful and gave him a small fine.
words.ex_cn: 法官很仁慈，只判了他一笔小额罚款。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as merciful, you mean that they show or have mercy.

words.ex: The judge showed mercy and let him go free.
words.ex_cn: 法官仁慈地让他自由了。
words.en: If someone in authority shows mercy, they choose not to harm someone they have power over, or they forgive someone they have the right to punish.

words.ex: It was a mere mistake, not intentional.
words.ex_cn: 那只是一个小小的错误，并非故意的。
words.en: You use mere to emphasize how unimportant or inadequate something is, in comparison to the general situation you are describing.

words.ex: He is merely a student.
words.ex_cn: 他仅仅是个学生。
words.en: You use merely to emphasize that something is only what you say and not better, more important, or more exciting.

words.ex: The two companies will merge next year.
words.ex_cn: 这两家公司明年将合并。
words.en: To combine or unite to form a single entity.

words.ex: The metallic spoon felt cold in her hand.
words.ex_cn: 金属勺子在她手中感觉很冷。
words.en: Metallic means relating to or resembling metal or metals.

words.ex: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
words.ex_cn: 把时间称为小偷是一种隐喻。
words.en: A metaphor is a figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

words.ex: The country uses metric units for weight and distance.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家使用米制单位来衡量重量和距离。
words.en: A metric is a system of measurement that uses meters, liters, and grams as its basic units.

words.ex: He lives in a big metropolis with many tall buildings.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个有很多高楼的大都市里。
words.en: A metropolis is a very large city, often the most important city in a country or area.

words.ex: The phone has a small microchip inside.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机里面有一个小芯片。
words.en: A microchip is a very small piece of silicon inside a computer. It has electronic circuits on it and can hold large amounts of information or perform mathematical and logical operations.

words.ex: He uses a microcomputer to do his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他用微型计算机做作业。
words.en: A microcomputer is a small computer that contains a microprocessor as its central processor.

words.ex: A microorganism can cause sickness.
words.ex_cn: 微生物会导致疾病。
words.en: A microorganism is a very small living thing that you can only see with a microscope.

words.tr: n. 微处理器；微处理机
words.ex: The computer has a fast microprocessor.
words.ex_cn: 这台电脑有一个快速的微处理器。
words.en: A microprocessor is a small chip that can process data and carry out instructions in a computer or other electronic device.

words.ex: She heated the food in the microwave.
words.ex_cn: 她把食物放在微波炉里加热。
words.en: A microwave is a type of oven that cooks or heats food very quickly by using electromagnetic waves rather than heat.

words.tr:
adj. 中途的；中间的
adv. 中途地；中间地
n. 娱乐场；游乐场
words.ex: He stopped midway to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他中途停下来休息。
